title: Warriors Trade Idea Swaps Podziemski for Elite Sharpshooter, Steven Adams
description: This Warriors trade sends Brandin Podziemski and Moses Moody to the Rockets in exchange for Reed Sheppard and Steven Adams. The post Warriors Trade Idea Swaps Podziemski for Elite Sharpshooter, Steven Adams appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Even the most loyal Golden State Warriors fan would admit that Brandin Podziemski hasn’t developed at the pace the franchise expected him to. At the end of his rookie season, the southpaw was widely heralded as Stephen Curry’s successor. Three years in, he has seemingly plateaued into an average rotational piece.

With Podz set to hit restricted free agency next year, the Warriors may be better off moving him before they have to grapple with a Jonathan Kuminga-type situation.

One Warriors trade idea doing the rounds would see the Bay Area franchise part with Podziemski and Moses Moody, who is expected to miss the first half of the 2026-27 season with injury, for a haul from the Houston Rockets.

Warriors would receive: Steven Adams, Reed Sheppard

Rockets would receive: Brandin Podziemski, Moses Moody

The hypothetical move stands to help both teams, as we explain below.

The return of Fred VanVleet from injury means Reed Sheppard will likely go back to a bench role after the young sharpshooter had a difficult playoff series against the Los Angeles Lakers. In the six-game series, the former No. 3 overall pick averaged 12.2 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.2 steals, but shot a paltry 30% from the field and 29% from three. While he averaged 32.2 minutes, Sheppard lost the faith of Rockets head coach Ime Udoka, who preferred to end games with either Tari Eason or Josh Okogie.

Much like the Warriors and Podz, the Rockets may run into a similar financial issue with Sheppard, who has only one more guaranteed year left before hitting restricted free agency in 2028. After extending Eason recently, the Rockets are also on the clock with Amen Thompson, who will hit restricted free agency in 2027.

Moody, who has two years left on a budget-friendly deal, isn’t a huge risk for the Rockets in this scenario. Ditto with Podz, whom they can simply waive next year.

Reed Sheppard has a lot of untapped potential, with some analysts projecting him to be an elite sharpshooter for years in the NBA. As a shooter, who better to harness your craft under than Stephen Curry, the greatest shooter in the history of the sport?

For all his flaws — including his defensive lapses and poor late-game decision-making — Sheppard is one of the purest young shooters in the NBA. In two seasons, he has drained 275 threes at a clip of 38.3% — elite numbers for a 22-year-old. A movement shooter who can also shoot off the dribble, he will fit nicely in Golden State’s system.

As for Steven Adams, the Warriors could use some interior presnece after finishing 22nd in rebounding and 26th in blocked shots last season. Adams will also bring the sort of toughness and physicality that the Warriors sorely miss when defensive anchor Draymond Green goes to the bench. In recent years, they’re unable to impose themselves defensively even when Green, 36, has been on the court.

title: Concerning Signs for Ben Shelton As Jack Draper Delivers a Reality Check During DC Open Practice
description: Ben Shelton’s preparations for the 2026 Mubadala DC Open have come under the microscope ahead of his highly anticipated campaign. After his first-round exit at Wimbledon, Shelton will look to bounce back strongly at the ATP 500 event on home soil, but his latest practice session with Jack Draper has raised concerns about his form ahead of his opening match.
fullText:
Ben Shelton’s preparations for the 2026 Mubadala DC Open have come under the microscope ahead of his highly anticipated campaign. After his first-round exit at Wimbledon, Shelton will look to bounce back strongly at the ATP 500 event on home soil, but his latest practice session with Jack Draper has raised concerns about his form ahead of his opening match.

Draper’s progress has repeatedly been derailed by injuries over the past few seasons, preventing him from building momentum on tour. After missing almost the entire clay-court season due to a knee injury, the Brit made a promising comeback on grass by reaching the semifinals of the Eastbourne Open under the guidance of his new coach, Andy Murray.

However, his injury woes resurfaced when an arm injury forced him to withdraw from Wimbledon. The Brit, who has slipped to world No. 147, has since accepted a wildcard for the DC Open and has been preparing for his return under Murray’s watchful eye.

Draper received an encouraging boost ahead of his opening match, defeating No. 2 seed Ben Shelton 6-1 in a practice session at the venue. Tennis reporter Christian’s Court revealed that Murray was pleased with the Brit’s dominant display.

On the other hand, the reporter flagged concerns about Shelton’s forehand looking below its usual standard.

“Draper just won a practice set 6-1 vs Shelton. Jack’s left arm and serve looked good; Coach Murray’s happy with his return too. Shelton’s FH has been very off though. Something to look out for next week,” the post read.

Shelton was originally scheduled to face fellow American Ethan Quinn in the first round of the DC Open. However, Quinn was forced to withdraw from the event due to a right metatarsal injury. The world No. 6 will now face either a qualifier or a lucky loser in his opening match.

MORE: Ben Shelton’s Girlfriend, Soccer Star Trinity Rodman, Joins Him at DC Open in Heartwarming Show of Support

Draper, meanwhile, will lock horns with Alex Michelsen in the first round of the ATP 500 event, marking their first tour-level encounter. If Draper emerges victorious, he will face the winner of the match between No. 5 seed Learner Tien and Adrian Mannarino in the second round.

Placed in opposite halves of the draw, Ben Shelton and Jack Draper will both need to reach the final to set up a blockbuster showdown at the DC Open. Their only previous meeting took place at the 2025 Indian Wells Masters, where Draper secured a 6-4, 7-5 victory.

title: New signing Steur features as Newcastle held to draw at Gateshead
description: Newcastle's summer signing Sean Steur played 90 minutes in Saturday's 1-1 draw at Gateshead.  Luke Supyk put the National League side ahead in the first-half and it was Ben Williams' own goal that pulled Eddie Howe's men level in the second.  In what was the Magpies first fan-facing friendly of the summer, Howe made lots of changes and Fabian Schar was back in action for the first time since he suffered an ankle injury in January.
fullText:
Newcastle's summer signing Sean Steur played 90 minutes in Saturday's 1-1 draw at Gateshead.

Luke Supyk put the National League side ahead in the first-half and it was Ben Williams' own goal that pulled Eddie Howe's men level in the second.

In what was the Magpies first fan-facing friendly of the summer, Howe made lots of changes and Fabian Schar was back in action for the first time since he suffered an ankle injury in January.

The Magpies midfield has been weakened by the departure of Sandro Tonali, who joined Tottenham this month in a deal worth up to £100m.

Young midfielders Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba have since arrived from Ajax and Monaco respectively.

Although Saturday's game came too soon for Bamba, whose move was announced on Friday, Steur played 90 minutes.

"He played really well today," Howe said. "He can be really pleased with his performance and first showing in Newcastle colours."

It is rare for an academy graduate to leave Ajax at 18, and for a fee worth up to £23m.

However, Newcastle have to take calculated risks before potential signings like Steur potentially explode in value and are out of reach.

Dutchman Steur clearly has promise.

There were glimpses of Steur's technical ability, composure and vision against National League side Gateshead.

But he will need time to adapt to the physicality and intensity of the Premier League.

Newcastle continue their pre-season preparations at Bristol City on Wednesday, 29 July (19:30 BST).

title: Strong Reactions Surface for Curtis Mead Trade to Red Sox: ‘Ideal Pairing’
description: The Red Sox sparked a mix of praise and skepticism for the Curtis Mead deal here. The post Strong Reactions Surface for Curtis Mead Trade to Red Sox: ‘Ideal Pairing’ appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Boston Red Sox left many fans theorizing that they would pull off an MLB Trade Deadline deal. Some even believed Tarik Skubal could wind up heading to Fenway Park. Boston indeed pulled off a trade Saturday night, sending left-handed pitcher Connelly Early to the Washington Nationals for third baseman Curtis Mead.

So Skubal remains with the Detroit Tigers in this move. But Boston sends out one of its own young pitchers to help boost the offense.

The Red Sox end up dumping a 24-year-old who was 8-7 overall as a starter, including posting a 7-5 mark in the 2026 season. Early also heads to the nation’s capital carrying a 3.44 ERA.

But the arrival of Mead sparked some strong reactions online, including one calling it an “ideal pairing.”

Yahoo Fantasy baseball analyst Corbin Young raved about the move on the social media website X, formerly known as Twitter.

“This should be an ideal pairing for the Red Sox,” Young posted.

Then the fantasy analyst dove into the stats attached to Mead that makes him impactful. Mead is “pulling the ball into the air 22.8% of the time this season, nearly four points higher than his career average” as Young pointed out.

He’s also “barreling the ball more” with a 7.5% barrel per PA, making it nearly three points higher than his career average.

Young isn’t the only one reacting to who the Red Sox are bringing in, though.

Unfortunately this is now the fourth time Mead gets shipped away in his MLB career. Boston happens to become his second 2026 playing destination, as he previously started out with the Chicago White Sox.

“It’s a big, big gamble on a monstrous small sample size this year, but there’s pedigree,” Boston Sports Gordo posted on X.

However, Draft Kings analyst Jordan Moore drew parallels with one notable move the franchise pulled off in 2018.

“Red Sox need right handed bat. Trade for Steve Pearce. He hit .288 with 11 HR, 42 RBI and wins World Series,” Moore said, noting that Mead is another right-handed hitter but has blasted more home runs (17) and RBIs (48) than when Pearce arrived ahead of that WS run.

Others believe this is Boston simply buying into the breakout wave Mead is currently on. With the intent that the Red Sox can ride his momentum during their current winning roll.

Boston flipped a winning switch in recent weeks.

The team tied its previous franchise best mark of 15 consecutive wins, tying the 1946 milestone. They’ve gone 8-2 overall in their last 10 games.

Furthermore, Boston now finds itself at 53-50 overall and in third place out in the American League East standings. But has a lot of catching up to do with the second-place New York Yankees and the division leading Tampa Bay Rays.

The AL East is hands down the toughest division in baseball, as the only place featuring three teams above .500 in the American League. Now Mead’s arrival could spark a further run for Boston.

title: Wilson makes Leeds debut in defeat by Wrexham
description: Wales attacking midfielder Harry Wilson makes his first outing for Leeds United as they are beaten 3-2 by Wrexham in the club's opening pre-season game.
fullText:
Wales attacking midfielder Harry Wilson made his first outing for Leeds United as they were beaten 3-2 by Wrexham in the club's opening pre-season game.

Wilson, who joined the Elland Road side on a free transfer in the summer after his contract at Fulham ran out, came on for the second half of the game at the Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.

Leeds found themselves behind almost immediately when Kieffer Moore put Wrexham in front in the first minute with a left-foot shot.

Joel Piroe had the chance to level from the spot after Dan James had been brought down by keeper Arthur Okonkwo, but missed with his penalty.

Piroe made amends for the Premier League side by equalising with a backheel from a Sean Longstaff ball.

Bailey Cadamarteri ran through on goal and slotted in to put Wrexham back in front before Leeds again levelled when Longstaff scored with a right-footed shot.

Wilson was introduced by Leeds manager Daniel Farke as part of his changes for a second half in which Sam Smith, who also scored Wrexham's winner in a pre-season victory against Manchester United, netted late on for the Championship side.

Leeds went close in added time through Wilson but his shot went over.

title: LAFC continues to surge in dominant showing against Sporting KC
description: Los Angeles remained perfect following the World Cup break, doing so in commanding fashion.
fullText:
Perhaps a few weeks of rest were all LAFC really needed to get back on track, with another wire-to-wire victory in the books. This time around, it was a 4-0 shutout performance against Sporting KC on Saturday evening, helping the Black & Gold secure three points for the fourth consecutive match.

Just like in Wednesday's win over Real Salt Lake, it was Son Heung-min and Denis Bouanga combining to provide the necessary fireworks in front of the home crowd. The duo combined for three scores on the night, helping LA set an emphatic tone early on.

It took Son less than five minutes to find the scoresheet, using his speed to get behind the Kansas City defense and meet a promising ball from Mark Delgado before tapping it calmly into the left side of the net.

THREE IN THREE FOR SON HEUNG-MIN!@LAFC lead within five minutes!

📺 Apple TV: https://t.co/QuMdm9OkRD pic.twitter.com/pYLoAqpBew

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

The 34-year-old has returned to action following the World Cup looking fresh with motivation, now having scored in each of the squad's three recent matches. LAFC, however, was only just beginning to make its mark on the scoresheet as a whole.

Bouanga had his turn next, using a burst of speed to make it 2-0 in the 37th minute. He followed Mathieu Choinière's lob all the way down the pitch, cleverly tapping it forward with his head and shooting past KC goalkeeper Stefan Cleveland.

Denis Bouanga strikes with lightning speed!

Blink and you might miss @LAFC's second goal. ⚡ pic.twitter.com/Yj3HntEsGZ

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

His ninth goal of the season served as the latest example of LAFC's recent effectiveness in transition. David Martínez found a goal of his own before the conclusion of the opening half, getting loose on a run down the pitch of his own and using a stop-and-start move to free himself for a strike from close range.

David Martinez nets @LAFC's third of the half!

The entire front three getting on the scoresheet in the opening 45 minutes. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/rsRSIh8hIc

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

Before the night's end, Bouanga ultimately struck once more to pocket a brace and secure double-digit goals on the season. Another long pass, this time from Ryan Porteous, landed at the feet of a running Tyler Boyd on the right side. His well-placed ball back toward Bouanga just inside the center of the box was enough for LA's leading scorer to make it 4-0.

Bouanga Brace!! 🚀@LAFC have scored 4️⃣! pic.twitter.com/V8pC2RIlMo

— Major League Soccer (@MLS) July 26, 2026

With the full-time whistle, LAFC improved to 10-5-3 overall, now tied atop the Western Conference table at 33 points with the Vancouver Whitecaps and San Jose Earthquakes. The Black & Gold also managed to continue their dominant stretch against KC in the process, now having gone unbeaten in their last 10 games against the club.

Since returning to play, LA has now scored 10 goals while conceding just one. Hugo Lloris earned his second clean sheet on Saturday since returning from the break, needing to make just one save.

LAFC will return to action seeking a fifth consecutive victory on Saturday, Aug. 1, heading north of the border to battle the Whitecaps in a clash of Western Conference leaders. The two sides have not squared off since the semifinals of the 2025 MLS Cup Playoffs, where Vancouver emerged victorious in a dramatic penalty shootout.

Kickoff is scheduled for 4:30 p.m. PT.

title: Barcelona activate operation to sign Premier League forward amid complications in Alvarez pursuit
description: Barcelona’s search for a new number nine has hit obstacle after obstacle this summer, with top target Julian Alvarez proving increasingly difficult to prise away from Atletico Madrid.That frustratio...
fullText:
Barcelona’s search for a new number nine has hit obstacle after obstacle this summer, with top target Julian Alvarez proving increasingly difficult to prise away from Atletico Madrid.

That frustration has forced Deco to explore alternatives, and one familiar name has now returned to the agenda.

Indeed, Barcelona have reactivated their interest in Eli Junior Kroupi as they look to solve their striker conundrum.

Eli Junior Kroupi is a viable option at Barcelona. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

According to Diario SPORT, Barcelona have once again put Kroupi’s name on the table, despite Bournemouth having previously declared the young Frenchman non-transferable.

With the Alvarez deal stalling due to Atletico’s refusal to negotiate, Deco has reopened the possibility of signing the France Under-21 international as one of the candidates to replace Robert Lewandowski.

The 20-year-old has enjoyed a superb debut campaign in the Premier League since joining from Lorient for €13 million, scoring 13 goals in 35 matches.

Those numbers have alerted a host of Europe’s biggest clubs, with Chelsea, PSG, Arsenal, Bayern Munich and Manchester City all credited with interest alongside Barcelona.

French but with Portuguese roots, Kroupi fits precisely the kind of profile Deco favours, and the sporting director remains keen despite the difficulties involved.

Eli Junior Kroupi has been identifed as an alternative to Alvarez. (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

The problem, however, is Bournemouth’s firm resistance. Football operations chief Tiago Pinto views Kroupi as the cornerstone of the club’s project and has made clear he will not sell this summer, reportedly not even for €100 million.

The Cherries are enjoying an exciting period, preparing for their European debut after a sixth-placed finish under Andoni Iraola, and are in no rush to part with one of their brightest assets.

To complicate matters further, agent Moussa Sissoko recently denied any negotiations with Barcelona.

Even so, Barcelona are keen to test whether that stance is truly final. With Alvarez looking a long shot and Flick eager for another striker, the club will continue to probe for openings, and Kroupi

title: Brandon Jennings Is Right: Jayson Tatum Took a Shot at Jaylen Brown
description: Jaylen Brown remained at the center of NBA conversation after the Boston Celtics sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers in a trade built around Paul George. Criticism of Boston’s return soon created a more personal question: Did the Celtics decide they could no longer manage Brown’s personality?Jayson Tatum then delivered a leadership lesson at an […] The post Brandon Jennings Is Right: Jayson Tatum Took a Shot at Jaylen Brown appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Jaylen Brown remained at the center of NBA conversation after the Boston Celtics sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers in a trade built around Paul George. Criticism of Boston’s return soon created a more personal question: Did the Celtics decide they could no longer manage Brown’s personality?

Jayson Tatum then delivered a leadership lesson at an event for The Jayson Tatum Foundation that sounded remarkably connected to the debate surrounding his former teammate, Yahoo reports.

“Being around somebody that feels like they know it all, I don’t wanna be around that person,” Tatum said. “I don’t wanna be the smartest person in the room, I want to learn from somebody else.”

Brandon Jennings did not accept that statement as generic guidance for young players. After reposting the clip on X, Jennings wrote, “Motivational message my a-s lmaooo that’s a shot at Jaylen Brown.”

Tatum never mentioned Brown, leaving room for another explanation. Still, Jennings’ conclusion fits the timing and familiar language too well to dismiss.

Motivational message my ass lmaooo that’s a shot at Jaylen Brown https://t.co/y7m1mcZpuW

— Brandon Jennings (@Tuff__Crowd) July 25, 2026

Fox Sports host Colin Cowherd previously said two NBA sources characterized Brown as a difficult locker room presence because of how highly he regards his own intelligence.

“He suddenly thinks he’s the smartest guy in every room he’s in,” Cowherd said. “You get into a really bad place.”

Brown rejected Cowherd’s premise during a livestream after the trade, USA Today reports. The 29-year-old argued that intelligence takes different forms and said he never viewed himself as the smartest person present. He then questioned the intellectual standard across the sports business.

“No offense to everybody in sports, but the bar is fu—– low,” Brown said. “You know what I mean. The bar isn’t that high.”

Brown aimed that criticism broadly, not specifically at Tatum. However, Tatum’s choice to warn against someone who “feels like they know it all,” then invoke the same smartest-person framing, made the comparison unavoidable.

Could Brown’s comment have irritated Tatum? No public statement proves it. Their separation still changes the dynamic. Brown no longer needs to smooth over every ambiguous remark for Boston’s locker room, and Tatum does not have to seek reassurance from a teammate who now plays for a conference rival.

Without that clarification, Tatum can interpret Brown’s words however he wants. Jennings merely said aloud what many viewers heard beneath the motivational packaging.

The basketball backdrop gives this exchange more weight. Tatum’s Achilles rehabilitation limited him to 16 regular-season appearances after the injury he sustained during the 2024-25 playoffs. He returned late and participated in Boston’s postseason run, apart from Game 7 against Philadelphia.

Brown carried a leading role during Tatum’s absence. Across 71 games, he set career highs with 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per contest. Brown also made the All-Star team, earned Second Team All-NBA recognition and ranked No. 6 in the MVP race.

That individual success did not produce Boston’s desired ending. The Celtics surrendered a 3-1 advantage against the 76ers, the team Brown later joined, and the collapse intensified scrutiny of his leadership as a primary option.

Tatum’s remarks do not confirm that he blamed Brown for Boston’s problems. They do, however, sound like a pointed response to the criticism that followed Brown out of Boston. Of every way Tatum could have discussed leadership, he selected language already attached to the loudest conversation about his former co-star.

That is why Jennings is right about the subtext. Until Tatum offers a different explanation, every Celtics-76ers meeting will invite another look at whether their long-running partnership ended with more friction than either star has acknowledged.

title: Bucs' Mayfield Shares Best Mental Advice He Has Ever Received
description: The Tampa Bay quarterback reveals how shedding pride and embracing vulnerability saved his career, offering a powerful reminder that no one has to face their struggles alone.
fullText:
Being a professional athlete not only requires an incredible amount of physical strength, but also mental strength.

Athletes must find a way to balance everything their jobs require with everything going on in their personal lives. The travel, diet discipline, being separated from loved ones, and the way they are treated by fans (both positively and negatively), among other things, are constant causes of stress that can't be escaped.

They also must learn how to handle both winning and losing, and have to worry that there will always be someone younger, cheaper, or possibly better, trying to take their spot.

Sometimes the physical requirements of the job cause an athlete to ignore his or her own mental health, and the results can be devastating.

In an excerpt from the Peak newsletter by The Athletic, Elise Devlin writes about the best piece of mental advice given to 13 professional athletes across many different sports.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers' quarterback Baker Mayfield was one of the athletes to offer what he believes has been the best advice he has ever received.

Mayfield told Devlin that the best thing he has ever learned is that it is ok to ask for help. Sometimes people (not just athletes) let their pride get the best of them and unnecessarily face problems alone instead of asking for help.

"Mayfield: I think asking for help is something that people feel ashamed of doing. But you have more people that care about you than you think. I’ve gone through things myself, and I’ve had teammates go through certain things, but you always have people in your corner."

It seems simple, but is something that many of us fail to take advantage of.

Mayfield has gone through a lot in his NFL career. He went from being the top overall pick in 2018 by the Cleveland Browns to being completely discarded, despite his success, only four years later.

His ugly divorce from the Browns, brought on by the team leaving him twisting in the wind as they pursued their ill-fated trade for Deshaun Watson, sent Mayfield's career on a downward spiral.

Mayfield spent the 2022 season between the Carolina Panthers and Los Angeles Rams as an afterthought whose time in the league, at least as a starter, looked to be nearing an end.

A player without strong mental health could have easily broken. Mayfield didn't.

Even when the Bucs gave him an opportunity to revive his career, it was only on a one-year contract for a small fraction of what starting QBs in the NFL make. He had to prove himself all over again.

Which he did. Mayfield threw for over 4,000 yards, 28 touchdowns, only 10 interceptions, and made his first Pro Bowl.

Mayfield had to use the advice he was given to make it through all of the drama from his Cleveland exit. He relied on others for the help he needed to overcome the challenges he was facing and now has the life experiences to help those around him who also need help.

Tampa is fortunate to have a quarterback as mentally strong as Mayfield.

title: Roma submit official bid for Israel Reyes

fullText:
Roma is looking for a Celik-style all-rounder, a player capable of playing across the right flank and even in a back-three, if necessary.

title: 👀 Police step in: this World Cup coach is getting (too) much hype
description: In Germany, people would certainly have been happy to reach the World Cup semi-finals, but for the England fans, given the way they were knocked out by Argentina, that was clearly not enough. Coach Th...
fullText:
In Germany, people would certainly have been happy to reach the World Cup semi-finals, but for the England fans, given the way they were knocked out by Argentina, that was clearly not enough. Coach Thomas Tuchel faced plenty of backlash.

Lionel Scaloni is currently experiencing the exact opposite, despite the disappointment of the final against Spain.

The Argentine coach is quite obviously perhaps even getting a little too much support from the fans.

Although he remains a hero to the fans despite the defeat, they have been crowding around his house for days. According to a report by ‘Tribuna.com’ and numerous videos on ‘X’, his house even had to be placed under police protection, and the authorities put up a fence around his property.

Numerous supporters of the Argentine national team have currently traveled to Scaloni’s hometown to meet their idol in person.

Police officers are now guarding the coach’s house around the clock, as the number of fans wanting to congratulate him or show their support keeps steadily growing.

Even though Argentina lost the final 1-0 to Spain, Scaloni has lost none of his popularity. Fans repeatedly gather outside his house, sing chants, and hope for photos or autographs.

According to reports, Scaloni comes out to the waiting supporters twice a day — in the morning and in the evening.

He greets them, signs autographs, and even watches small performances that fans put on outside his house.

So the bond between coach and fans cannot be broken even by a lost final — at the same time, of course, it is important that things do not become too intense and that the Argentine manager eventually gets some time to catch his breath again.

title: 'Chaos' & 'madness' - where does Joshua win leave Fury fight?
description: What does Anthony Joshua's chaotic comeback win over Kristian Prenga leave the super-fight with Tyson Fury?
fullText:
After just 20 seconds, the biggest fight in British boxing had seemingly gone up in smoke in Jeddah's desert air.

Anthony Joshua was flat on his back and a long-awaited showdown with Tyson Fury was hanging in the balance.

One more knockdown, one astonishing comeback and a second-round knockout later, the blockbuster bout was revived.

But after one of the wildest nights of Joshua's career against Kristian Prenga, the Fury fight suddenly feels like a very different contest.

"That was chaos. Absolute chaos. Just madness," former cruiserweight world champion Tony Bellew said on DAZN.

Joshua's emotional win over Prenga in pictures

Relive Joshua's dramatic comeback knockout win

Bloodied Kelly battles past Agyarko to retain title

The emotion of Joshua's comeback victory cannot be overstated. Given everything he has endured since the tragic car crash in Nigeria that claimed the lives of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele, simply stepping back into the ring was an achievement.

Sentiment aside, though, had Albanian Prenga pressed home his advantage after dropping Joshua twice in the opening round, the story could have been very different.

Prenga arrived with an impressive record - 20 knockouts from 20 victories and one defeat - but had never operated anywhere near this level or under this kind of spotlight.

"I think we need to look at that first round and look at how easily AJ was hurt. We can't just skip past that," 5 Live boxing pundit Steve Bunce said.

"We saw a man in a very bad place come through an even worse situation and emerge victorious at the end. That will be the story.

"However, once we step back, we need to keep looking at that first round and start asking: how much further do we want to push him?"

This was supposed to be Joshua's comeback week. Instead, Fury reminded everyone that he remains the master of stealing a headline.

Fury was originally expected to fight on 1 August in Dublin, but moved quickly to schedule his own bout against a 46-year-old Mariusz Wach for the evening before Joshua's fight night.

Then in fight week came the usual Fury theatre. He insisted he would not be in Jeddah, before hinting the opposite. An Instagram post tagged with the location "Who Knows" only added fuel to the speculation.

In the end, Fury stayed away and perhaps that was a blessing for Joshua. Had Fury been sitting ringside watching his rival get dropped twice in the opening round, would Joshua have found the same reserves of determination to turn the fight around? Would the pressure of knowing Fury was watching have changed the moment?

We will never know. But what we do know is that while the two men made it through their respective warm-ups, questions remain after both performances.

Fury's seventh-round victory over Wach was heavily criticised by some but it was effectively a public sparring session designed to keep Fury active and keep his name in the conversation.

There was little jeopardy involved and Fury appeared to be enjoying himself, even sharing a playful moment by kissing his opponent on the head.

Perhaps we should read more into his performance against Arslanbek Makhmudov in April where Fury - while still showing signs of decline - looked comfortable and controlled.

Fury's greatest weapon has always been his ability to expose hesitation, vulnerability and mistakes - and Joshua showed all three against Prenga.

In the aftermath of such a chaotic night, it is easy to focus only on the flaws and forget the bigger picture. Joshua was returning from one of the darkest periods of his life and carrying an immense emotional burden into the ring.

After his hand was raised, he struggled to get through his interview. His voice cracked as he spoke about his two friends and the impact their loss has had on him.

"Boxing once saved him and he needed boxing to get through this. That camp allowed him to focus his mind while he was in so much grief and pain," promoter Eddie Hearn said.

"You don't know what he was going through in that camp because he doesn't talk about it."

Whatever happens next, his place in British boxing history is already secure. He is an Olympic gold medallist, a two-time heavyweight champion and one of the biggest sporting stars this country has produced.

He has taken boxing to places few British fighters ever have. He has filled stadiums, headlined global events and become a household name far beyond the sport.

But in the build-up to his comeback, Joshua and his stablemate Oleksandr Usyk spoke about the ambition of becoming undisputed heavyweight champion.

After Saturday night in Saudi, the reality is that even reclaiming a world title would be a tough ask.

Joshua has always spoken about legacy, and there would be something fitting about walking away after overcoming one of the toughest periods of his life and producing a dramatic comeback victory.

The danger with ageing fighters is chasing one more night. Boxing history is filled with champions who stayed that one fight too long.

But then again Fury-Joshua is not one more fight. It is the fight. The one that has loomed over their careers for the best part of a decade.

title: Report: Spurs star courted by Serie A giants as director confirms interest
description: Cristian Romero to Inter Milan? Tottenham Face Defining Calls on Captain, Vicario and Summer Attack PlansTottenham’s summer is starting to take on a familiar shape, big names attracting serious inte...
fullText:
Tottenham’s summer is starting to take on a familiar shape, big names attracting serious interest, a squad in transition, and a head coach making little effort to disguise where he wants action next. According to Sky Sports, Inter Milan are interested in a move for Cristian Romero, with the Italian champions exploring whether a deal for the Spurs captain can be made to work during this window.

On the face of it, that possibility feels significant. Romero remains one of Tottenham’s highest-profile players, a World Cup-winning defender who has often embodied both the best and most volatile aspects of the club over recent years. Inter’s admiration is understandable, particularly as they seek to reinforce at centre-back, but the report makes clear that any agreement would be financially complex.

That point matters. Romero is under contract until 2029, he remains a premium-level defender when fit, and Tottenham are under no immediate contractual pressure. Yet there is also said to be an expectation that Spurs would sanction a sale if the right offer arrives. In a market where elite central defenders are scarce, that wording feels important. It suggests this is not an untouchable asset, it is a situation to watch.

Inter are understood to be looking for a central defender this summer and Romero is among the names under consideration, along with John Stones, now a free agent after departing Manchester City. That gives context to their search. They are not scanning the market for developmental options, they are looking at proven pedigree and immediate quality.

For Tottenham, Romero’s profile means there would be no shortage of debate if negotiations advanced. He has made 124 appearances across five seasons, contributed 12 goals, and collected four Premier League red cards, a record that neatly captures the mix of front-foot aggression and occasional recklessness that has defined his time in north London.

There is also the wider backdrop to consider. Romero missed the end of last season with a knee injury and became a source of frustration among supporters amid the noise around a possible attendance at Belgrano’s final against River Plate, at a time when Tottenham were fighting for Premier League survival. He did make it to Spurs’ final match of the season, but the episode added another layer to an already nuanced relationship between player and fanbase.

None of that diminishes his footballing value. Fully fit, Romero is still the kind of defender top clubs notice. He is aggressive in duels, front-footed in recovery situations and comfortable taking responsibility in possession. But if Tottenham are open to the right offer, this may come down to whether they believe this is the optimum moment to cash in and reshape.

Even with the Romero situation developing in the background, the messaging from Roberto De Zerbi on the club’s priorities has been direct. Tottenham have already committed £237m on six signings in an extraordinary window by their own standards, headlined by Sandro Tonali’s £100m arrival from Newcastle, £85m for Mateus Fernandes and £52m for Jan Paul van Hecke. Andy Robertson, Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka have also joined on free transfers.

De Zerbi has now publicly shifted attention to the final phase of the window. As he put it, “The target now is to complete the attacking positions.” He also said, “We want the first target, the first level, because anyway we are already important players, but I think to start the new project we need another couple of important players, for sure.”

There is little ambiguity there. Tottenham’s recruitment drive has addressed multiple areas, but the head coach wants two attacking additions of genuine level, not squad fillers. He reinforced that message by adding, “It’s not finished yet, our transfer market window. We have to finish, we have to bring another couple of, maybe more, maybe not less, but a couple of players.”

That is the language of a coach who sees a clear gap between where the squad is now and where he believes it needs to be by the start of the season. Whether that is funded purely through existing resources or accelerated by departures such as Romero will be one of the key themes of the coming weeks.

Romero is not the only notable Spurs player with uncertainty around his future. Juventus are again considering Guglielmo Vicario as an alternative option as they work through their goalkeeping shortlist. The Italian club are also exploring a move for Parma’s Zion Suzuki, with the valuation gap there thought to be manageable, but Vicario remains firmly in the conversation.

Vicario is expected to leave this summer and has not travelled on pre-season tour because of what De Zerbi described as a minor injury. The Spurs head coach said: “Vicario is injured, not a big injury, but he needs to stay one week in London.” That may be routine on the surface, but in a transfer window, every absence attracts scrutiny, particularly when a player is already linked with an exit.

Lucas Bergvall is another case that speaks to the scale of Tottenham’s churn. The Sweden midfielder is understood to want to move on this summer, with Nottingham Forest still engaged and Newcastle having discussed figures with Spurs. Despite club sources maintaining they do not want to sell, there has reportedly been no push to persuade him to stay.

De Zerbi’s stance is practical rather than emotional. He said: “I have not spoken with Lucas yet. I will in the next days and we will make the best decision for the club, for Lucas, for me, for every one of us. Without problems, Lucas is a big, big talent.” He then added, “There will be a big competition to play because at the end, I think we will be two players for each position. If he wants to stay, I will be happy. Otherwise, we have to find a new solution with Johan Lange, with Vinai. It’s not my business after the decision to leave.”

That is a revealing insight into the current Spurs model. The head coach wants commitment, the sporting department wants clarity, and if a player is minded to go, the club appear increasingly willing to seek a clean resolution.

There is some positive fitness news for Tottenham amid the transfer noise. Mohammed Kudus is nearing a return after a muscle injury that has kept him out since early January. De Zerbi said: “Kudus is very close. I think when we come back to London he will be available to start working with us. It’s a great thing for us. Kudus is another important player.”

That update matters, particularly given the head coach’s insistence on adding more attacking quality. Kudus returning to training would feel like a major internal reinforcement, even if it does not change the broader objective of recruiting two more forwards. Tottenham need depth, but they also need difference-makers, and a fit Kudus clearly falls into that category.

There was a more cautious note on Dejan Kulusevski, with the club determined not to rush his comeback after a long period without playing. De Zerbi explained: “Kulusevski, we have to see in the next couple of weeks. He’s another important player. After one season, one complete season, without a game, we have to analyse better and better, don’t take risks, first of all for him and then for us.”

title: £128m Richard Hughes disaster-class comes back to haunt Liverpool
description: Richard Hughes' summer transfer window last term was expected to change things for Liverpool.He spent over £450 million on new players in an attempt to help the Reds retain their Premier League title...
fullText:
Richard Hughes' summer transfer window last term was expected to change things for Liverpool.

He spent over £450 million on new players in an attempt to help the Reds retain their Premier League title and potentially win the Champions League.

And, on paper, the additions of Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak promised to do exactly that but, for one reason or another, that isn't how things panned out.

They were knocked out in the round of 16 of the Champions League and they also only managed to finish in fifth place which, after their massive summer of spending, was far from ideal.

These poor performances led to fans demanding that new players were brought in and even made some of the Liverpool players decide they were better off elsewhere.

Of all the departures though, Mohamed Salah's is the one that has hit Liverpool the hardest and, no matter what Hughes tries to do, he can't seem to rectify it with another one of his disaster-classes feeling like it's about to arise.

Yan Diomande was the player who most Liverpool fans thought would be brought in to replace Salah.

Even before the summer transfer window opened, the Ivorian was being linked with an Anfield switch with Liverpool briefing most media outlets that he was their number one target.

In the end, however, Diomande chose against making a Liverpool switch and it was reported that he'd prefer his next move to be Paris Saint-Germain.

So, from then on, there was only really the Parisians being linked with a move but, since hardly any movement has been made regarding the deal, other clubs are starting to join the race and now, according to Fabrizio Romano, Real Madrid are 'in talks' with RB Leipzig about a potential move for the attacker.

"Manchester City have gone quiet on Yan Diomande days ago after calls to check the situation, same for Arsenal," he wrote.

"Diomande has only opened doors to Real Madrid since he agreed personal terms with Paris Saint-Germain in June.

"Real Madrid now in club to club talks with Leipzig."

After Liverpool were told that Diomande didn't want to join them, their focus instantly changed towards making a move for Bradley Barcola.

A deal for the Frenchman made a lot of sense, if PSG were going to sign Diomande then Barcola would be put even further down the pecking order than he already is.

This would lead to even more fallings-out between the 23-year-old and Luis Enrique which is why the Reds made him their main target.

However, now that Diomande isn't likely to join PSG, there's no way that the Ligue 1 outfit will let him go.

PSG were already digging their heels in and were asking for around £128 million to allow him to leave but, now that their deal for Diomande looks likely to be off, there's no reason for them to move him on, unless they can't get him to agree to a new contract, of course.

There are obviously still a lot of moving parts in each of these deals so anything could end up happening but, if Hughes continues waiting around to agree a deal for Barcola, it could end up being another disaster-class for the sporting director.

That is, especially if they don't end up adding anymore attackers to their ranks this summer.

title: Spence Jr to retire after losing comeback fight
description: Former welterweight world champion Errol Spence Jr will retire from boxing after losing his comeback fight to Tim Tszyu in Sydney.
fullText:
Former welterweight world champion Errol Spence Jr has retired from boxing after losing his comeback fight to Tim Tszyu in Sydney.

American Spence Jr, 36, held the WBA, WBC and IBF belts and was undefeated in 28 fights before being beaten by Terence Crawford three years ago.

His first fight back saw him on the back foot throughout against Australian Tszyu, losing 118-110, 117-111, 117-111 on points.

"I think yeah, for sure," Spence said when asked if this was the end of the road for his career.

"I've got my faculties intact. My money is good at working for itself. Everything's good, man.

"I've got a beautiful family, and I thank God I'm gracious to leave this sport with my faculties intact and my family still by my side."

Tszyu grew in confidence and power throughout the fight and consistently looked to attack Spence's chin. He now wants a shot at a title of his own.

"I had sleepless nights thinking about, 'What am I going to feel like facing a legend like that?' But it was one hell of a show, and I understand why he's one of the greats," Tszyu said.

"I'd love to fight for a title. That's what I'm aiming for. But I've got to say beating a great like Errol Spence tops a world title."

Spence won his first title in 2017 when he beat British fighter Kell Brook at Bramall Lane.

title: Tim Tszyu outlasts Errol Spence Jr. as an era ends in Sydney
description: Tim Tszyu turned back a legend in his own backyard, outworking Errol Spence Jr. over twelve rounds for a unanimous decision that closed the book on Spence's career. Full round-by-round and quotes from Afterpay Arena.
fullText:
SYDNEY — Errol Spence Jr. came to Afterpay Arena chasing one more run at glory. He left it as a fighter who fought his heart out and still walked away with nothing but respect, a unanimous decision loss to Tim Tszyu, and the rest of his life ahead of him. Tszyu (28-3, 18 KOs), the hometown superstar, took a fight that swung wildly across twelve rounds and closed it out the way champions do: on his terms, in front of his people, with the job finished against a fighter of Spence's (28-2, 22 KOs) caliber.

The card wasn't supposed to look like this. Stephen Fulton Jr. vs. Liam Wilson was pulled after Fulton missed weight, and PBC scrambled to slot in unbeaten light heavyweights Paulo Aokuso and Luis Antonio Tejeda as the opener instead. It bumped the streaming prelims entirely and pushed the pay-per-view straight into action, but by the time Spence and Tszyu made their walks, none of that mattered. Both men were locked in at 159 pounds, and Afterpay Arena was rocking.

Tim Tszyu made his entrance first, fire and pyro lighting up the arena as Jimmy Lennon Jr. worked the mic. Errol Spence Jr. followed with his team a few minutes later, the calm before a storm nobody could have scripted.

Round one belonged to Tszyu almost immediately. He landed upstairs and wobbled Spence, who was working the body early but looked shaken every time Tszyu found the head. It was a warning shot for what was coming.

Tim Tszyu connects early up top on Errol Spence Jr. with a right hand that found a home for a majority of the fight.

Spence answered how he always has, digging to the body and mixing in power shots, and by round three he was landing over the top after softening Tszyu underneath. But Tszyu kept walking forward, refusing to be discouraged, and his corner had a message between rounds: make Spence fight your fight, not his. Round four belonged to Tszyu again as he found his rhythm to the body, flipping the script on the fighter who'd built his legacy doing exactly that.

Tim Tszyu's right hand finds an opening and lands cleanly on the chin of Errol Spence Jr. at Afterpay Arena in Sydney, Australia.

Rounds seven through nine were where the fight tipped. Tszyu's sweeping right hand landed with increasingly perfect timing, his jab opened up the head, and the broadcast crew didn't hide it: Spence looked like a man in deep water who didn't want to be there anymore. Spence kept trying to answer downstairs, but Tszyu absorbed it and fired back with hard counters, closing round nine with backhand hooks and a straight right that snapped Spence's head back.

A right hand from Tim Tszyu snaps Errol Spence Jr.'s head back during their middleweight bout Saturday night at Afterpay Arena in Sydney.

Spence found one more gear late. He dug in during round eleven, trading upstairs with Tszyu and stealing the round on will alone, the heart of a former champion who wasn't ready to let go just yet. It wasn't enough. Round twelve was all Tszyu, setting up the jab and working the body over and over while Spence had nothing left to answer with. The crowd roared him home in the final twenty seconds.

The fight went the full twelve rounds, and the scorecards reflected just how much Tszyu took over as it wore on: 118-110, 117-111, 117-111, all in favor of Tim Tszyu by unanimous decision.

Tim Tszyu raises his hand in victory after defeating Errol Spence Jr. by unanimous decision in Sydney, Australia.

“Middleweight is my new division and I feel strong,” Tszyu said afterward. “This was one hell of a show. There were sleepless nights where I was thinking about facing a legend like Spence. I understand why he's one of the greats.” He credited his corner and trainer Jeff Fenech for the gameplan, saying he's chasing the standard set by his father, Kostya Tszyu, and Fenech both.

“I'd love to fight for a world title. I want Erislandy Lara and all the champions,” Tszyu said, already looking toward his next move. “But beating a great like Errol Spence tops any world title for me.”

Tim Tszyu and Errol Spence Jr. embrace in the ring after the final bell, finally sharing a handshake after a promotion defined by tension between the two.

For Spence, the moment carried far more finality. “It was a good fight and congratulations to Tim,” Spence said. “It's been a great event and everyone has treated me well. I answered a lot of questions for myself and now it's time to go home with my family and start a new life. I've got my faculties intact and my money is working for itself. I'm thankful to leave this sport with my family by my side.”

Errol Spence Jr. retires from boxing after this fight, closing the book on one of the more talented careers of his generation on a night that, fittingly, went the distance.

title: Opinion: Liverpool should now look at Real Madrid star
description: Liverpool Transfer Latest: Endrick in Focus as Barcola Uncertainty BuildsLiverpool’s summer window has entered what Dave Davis described on Anfield Index as the “winger Wild West”, with uncertai...
fullText:
Liverpool’s summer window has entered what Dave Davis described on Anfield Index as the “winger Wild West”, with uncertainty growing around the club’s attacking plans and fresh attention falling on Endrick as an alternative worth considering.

Speaking on the latest Anfield Index discussion, Davis captured the mood around the fanbase and the market in equal measure. “It feels like the transfer market has become the winger Wild West,” he said, before adding that “Liverpool and Richard Hughes may have already got the hell out of dodge is the worry as well.”

That sense of agitation has been fuelled by the latest developments around Bradley Barcola, PSG, and Real Madrid’s push for Xavi Simons. The concern raised in the discussion was straightforward. If Simons does not move to PSG, does that lessen the prospect of Barcola becoming available?

According to the discussion, Liverpool’s priorities remain clear in public terms, attacking reinforcement, and defensive cover. Yet the most urgent focus centred on wide options, and on whether the club’s preferred route is now beginning to narrow.

There was no attempt to disguise the issue. “The ultimate thing that people are getting down to is this is just the truth,” Davis said. “Earlier in the summer, we had hopes of Diomande and Barcola coming through the door. Now, well, there’s not going to be Diomande, who we’ll talk about. And there’s a possibility it might not even be Barcola with latest developments at the same time as well.”

The changing picture around Real Madrid and Xavi Simons was presented as one of the biggest market shifts of the last 24 hours. In turn, it has prompted renewed questions over whether PSG would sanction a sale of Barcola without further incoming business.

Davis was careful not to declare the pursuit over, but he was equally clear on the implications. “Does this definitively mean, definitively, that Bradley Barcola is staying at Paris? No. It ain’t helpful though, is it?”

For now, there remains time, a point Davis returned to more than once. “The window doesn’t shut until the 1st of September,” he said, while later repeating, “there is still time.” But the concern around pace and execution is now part of the conversation.

Among the names discussed, Endrick drew the strongest analytical focus. Davis made it plain that if Liverpool are forced to pivot, the Real Madrid forward is one option he would seriously consider.

“For me, go Brazilian,” he said. “There’s two real options here. Go Brazilian.” The first of those was Endrick.

Davis then laid out the case in direct terms. “Endrick wants to stay at Real Madrid despite the difficulty of getting minutes, but at Real Madrid, they don’t rule out a possible departure this summer.” He followed that with the numbers cited in the discussion, “He went to Lyon at the start of 2026 for a 6-month loan. I mean, look at that. 1,732 minutes, eight goals, eight assists.”

While Endrick was the priority name within the discussion, Davis also outlined another Brazilian route if Barcola proves unattainable. “We’ve already looked at Rayan before,” he said. “He would can jump at the chance to move to Liverpool.”

His position on that option was also direct. “If it’s not Barcola, I’d just be going and getting Rayan. It’s getting like that in the market.”

Still, Endrick was clearly the standout from the segment, largely because he was discussed with the most detail around role, production and suitability. In the context of a market Davis repeatedly described as chaotic, Liverpool may soon need exactly that kind of clarity.

There was, however, an effort to maintain perspective. Amid the transfer anxiety, Davis urged supporters not to spiral. “Let’s not be hitting any panic buttons just yet,” he said. Later, he added, “No one likes the word patience, but it is needed.”

That reflects where things stand. Liverpool are still being framed as looking for “an attacker, maybe attackers plural, and a defender”, but the mood has shifted because others are moving while their own business remains unresolved.

Davis summed it up neatly when he said, “People aren’t moaning. We’re asking questions.”

That is where Liverpool find themselves heading into the next stage of the window. Barcola remains uncertain, Endrick has entered the conversation in a meaningful way, and the market around elite wide players is shifting quickly. For now, the story is one of waiting, watching, and preparing for a possible pivot.

title: Today’s Papers: Fonbet row halts Pirlo coronation, Spalletti eyes Kolo Muani
description: Andrea Pirlo dominates Sunday’s front pages, but his move to become Italy head coach has hit an unexpected snag.La Gazzetta dello Sport splashes on ‘Russian shadows’, reporting that FIGC preside...
fullText:
Andrea Pirlo dominates Sunday’s front pages, but his move to become Italy head coach has hit an unexpected snag.

La Gazzetta dello Sport splashes on ‘Russian shadows’, reporting that FIGC president Giovanni Malagò wants to clarify the coach’s ties to Fonbet, a Moscow-based betting firm for whom Pirlo has served as global ambassador, before any deal is signed.

Pirlo’s lawyers insist the link runs through his current club, United FC Dubai, whose owner Sergey Lomakin holds interests in the company, and would lapse automatically, without penalty, once he leaves the Emirates.

The Corriere dello Sport goes harder, declaring that ‘Pirlo splits Italy’. It frames Paolo Maldini’s pick as a gamble that has left clubs, supporters and politicians cold, with sports minister Andrea Abodi among those voicing reservations even as he offered a measured “I’m rooting for him”.

Antonio Conte and Roberto Mancini linger in the background should the federation waver. Tuttosport strikes the same note under ‘Russian sponsor, then Abodi: Pirlo’s thorns’.

Away from the national team, Tuttosport leads on Luciano Spalletti, who oversaw a 1-0 friendly win at Standard Liège through a Fabio Miretti strike.

“I’m waiting for Kolo!” runs the headline, a nod to the coach’s push to land Randal Kolo Muani, with Eljif Elmas, a Scudetto winner under Spalletti at Napoli, also floated. The paper adds that Loïs Openda is bound for Lyon, João Mário is edging towards Fiorentina, and Liverpool have moved for Conceição.

Inter feature prominently too. The Corriere reports the pursuit of Cristian Romero is advancing, with Oaktree ready to fund a €40m package to satisfy Tottenham, while Yann Bisseck has signed a renewal through 2031.

Napoli, meanwhile, face noise around Romelu Lukaku, whose agent warns the striker “won’t be a reserve” as the club chase a defender, with Tiago Gabriel in pole. Roma have tabled €30m plus bonuses for Bologna’s Santiago Castro.

title: 'Think about cricket, not social media': Ishan Kishan to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
description: Ishan Kishan praised young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after India's T20 win. He believes the 15-year-old possesses match-winning qualities for the national team. Senior players are guiding Sooryavanshi to focus solely on his cricket. They encourage him to ignore social media and external distractions. Kishan highlighted Sooryavanshi's attacking style as a significant team asset.
fullText:
Kishan'c comments came after India's 90-run win over Zimbabwe in the second T20I in Harare on Saturday. India were in early trouble after losing Abhishek Sharma (8) and Sooryavanshi (20) inside the first three overs, slipping to 29/2. Kishan then played a brilliant knock of 81 off 44 balls to guide India to 219/5. Zimbabwe were later bowled out for 129 as India sealed the three-match series 2-0 with one game to spare.

Kishan said the senior members of the squad are helping Sooryavanshi settle into international cricket and are encouraging him to ignore distractions away from the game.

"Vaibhav is actually very smart. He knows what he is doing," Kishan said after India's win.

"He knows how he has to bat and how he has to carry himself on and off the field."

The wicketkeeper-batter revealed that he, Abhishek Sharma, captain Axar Patel and other experienced players regularly speak to the youngster to ensure he remains focused.

"When you represent India, you have to know what to focus on," he said.

"Me, Abhishek, Axar bhai and many others keep telling him to think about cricket, not social media or outside noise."

Kishan said the team wants Sooryavanshi to learn from the experiences of the senior players and avoid getting distracted early in his career.

"When you have such a player and you know that he is very young, you will never want him to be distracted for the wrong reasons.

"So our job as a team, we are like brothers and he comes from my place, so we just have to be happy, focus on the important things. The mistakes we have made in our starting, he should not do that. He should enjoy his cricket, like he is doing now."

Kishan believes Sooryavanshi's attacking style can have a major impact on India's performances.

"If he stays on the pitch, the difference he can create for the team is huge. A player who can attack from the first ball can take you to 80-90 runs in the powerplay," he said.

title: Kane: An Honor to Play for Red Wings
description: The post Kane: An Honor to Play for Red Wings appeared first on Detroit Hockey Now. In his first official reappearance with the Chicago Blackhawks, Patrick Kane came to praise the Detroit Red Wings. And he […] The post Kane: An Honor to Play for Red Wings appeared first on Detroit Hockey Now.
fullText:
The post Kane: An Honor to Play for Red Wings appeared first on Detroit Hockey Now.

In his first official reappearance with the Chicago Blackhawks, Patrick Kane came to praise the Detroit Red Wings.

He started on the right track. Kane acknowledged what his three seasons wearing the legendary winged wheel had meant to him.

— Patrick Kane (@88PKane) July 25, 2026

“It was truly an honor to be a Red Wing, and I enjoyed every minute of it,” Kane said in a post on his X feed. “To be part of such a storied franchise and to be welcomed with open arms is something my family and I will never forget.”

Kane took time to thank the Ilitch family, owners of the Red Wings. He bid farewell to many of his longtime Detroit teammates.

“To Larks, Mo, Razor, Ras, Copper, JT, and Benny, thank you for being amazing teammates and trying to pull the most out of me and our team everyday,” Kane said.

Kane saved special praise for his closest ally in the Red Wings locker room.

“To be able to play with Alex DeBrincat again, one of my best friends in hockey, and watch our sons develop a similar friendship was incredible,” Kane said. “You’re an amazing player and person, and I cherished our time together on and off the ice.”

Then Kane began discussing his future with the Blackhawks, and well, things took a turn.

It wasn’t so much what Kane said about the Red Wings that was the tell. It was the words he was attaching to the hopefulness he sees ahead for the Blackhawks.

“Obviously the story’s great, coming back to Chicago and being a Blackhawk again and kinda where I spend my summers and Chicago being my home, I think all that is great,” Kane said at his introductory press conference on his return to the Blackhawks.

As the Patrick Kane signing as sunk in more as the day has gone on, I keep thinking of him watching the tribute video his first game back in Chicago with Detroit.

He was going through it and it was written all over his face. Typically you get the smile and wave, maybe wipe a… pic.twitter.com/3QYAyVP4Hw

— Duke Coughlin (@ThatPodGuyDuke) July 23, 2026

“But I think, most importantly, it was about coming to a team where I think I can fit in well. A team that’s on the rise. A team that’s looking to make some big steps forward and try to make the playoffs.”

Bottom line? Kane sees a bright future in Chicago. A future that, evidently, he didn’t see in Detroit.

title: ScreenFocus – keyboard focus follows the pointer across Mac displays
description: A native macOS menu-bar utility that aligns keyboard focus with the display under your pointer. - therohitdas/ScreenFocus
fullText:
A small native macOS utility that keeps keyboard focus aligned with the display
 containing your pointer.

Rohit Das · macOS 14+ ·
 Apple Silicon and Intel · SwiftUI + AppKit · No analytics

ScreenFocus lives in the menu bar. When your pointer crosses to another display,
it immediately highlights that display and moves keyboard focus to the window
under the pointer—without requiring a click.

If there is no usable window under the pointer, ScreenFocus temporarily takes
focus itself. Ordinary typing no longer reaches a text field on the previous
display, while system-wide shortcuts from macOS, Raycast, Karabiner-Elements,
and Logitech software remain available.

On macOS, moving the pointer to another display does not move keyboard focus.
That makes it easy to press a shortcut over Display 2 and accidentally run it
inside an editor that is still focused on Display 1. ScreenFocus closes that gap.

title: Source Code Grep: Use your own grep, but make it source code aware
description: A blazing-fast, source-code-aware `grep` wrapper. Searches only real source files and skips build artifacts, binaries, vendor dirs etc. Respects `.gitignore` file. - m-manu/scgrep
fullText:
grep-like commands on unix-like OSes are great. They come pre-installed. In fact, a search using grep is faster than
the search on your IDE when there is no code index.

But, one key pain when using grep for searching in your source code or configuration files? A grep -r scans all
files (including binary files 🫣) and not just source code files, making it slow. Sometimes, very slow.

scgrep, which stands for 'source code grep', is a lightweight CLI tool that wraps your system's
grep command and runs it only on source code files. Flags and pattern you pass to scgrep are passed as is to the
underlying grep command, making it almost 100% compatible with grep. So, no need to learn a new syntax!

scgrep runs not one but multiple grep commands in parallel, making it significantly faster on large directories.

scgrep provides a specific flag --directories that lets you specify multiple directories

Note: Order matters for --directories (everything after --directories is treated as a directory path)

A bare -- ends grep's own flag parsing. Useful when the pattern starts with a -.

If the chosen command is not on PATH (or the absolute path does not exist), scgrep exits with code 6 and does not
run a search.

scgrep doesn't reimplement the logic to ignore files in .gitignore in a git repo. It relies on underlying git
command instead. If git is not installed or is not in $PATH, scgrep uses its default source-code awareness
behavior.

These tools reimplement the grep logic, in their own ways. In many cases, they're not compatible with grep.

scgrep acts as a thin wrapper and lets you use your own grep and just adds source-code awareness.

scgrep command traverses file tree with source code awareness in following ways:

Additionally, when git is available and the search root is inside a Git working tree, scgrep respects the
.gitignore file (via git ls-files).

Flags such as -r, -R and --recursive get ignored. scgrep passes these flags as is to the underlying grep,
which ignores these flags because underlying grep receives list of file names (not directories) as arguments.

e.g. Output of scgrep -r -i "TODO" would be same as scgrep -i "TODO"

title: If another civilisation lived on Earth before us, would we know?
description: When astrobiologist Adam Frank walked into the office of NASA scientist Gavin Schmidt, he had what he believed was the weirdest question: do aliens experience climate change?
fullText:
When astrobiologist Adam Frank walked into the office of NASA scientist Gavin Schmidt, he had what he believed was the weirdest question: do aliens experience climate change?

It took just moments for Schmidt to out-weird him.

Frank, a University of Rochester professor who looks for signs of life in the universe, was digging into whether advanced civilisations would inevitably trigger climate shifts, just as humans are doing now.

He was looking at other planets, he told Schmidt that day back in 2017, "because, of course, we know that there have been no other civilisations on Earth."

Schmidt immediately cut him off. "How do you know that?" he asked.

It was a record scratch moment, Frank said, and it started the two scientists off on an investigation. If an advanced civilisation had lived on Earth millions of years ago, powered themselves with energy and wiped themselves out, would we know? Would they have left traces of their presence etched into the record of our planet?

They called the idea the "Silurian hypothesis" - after a fictional advanced race of reptiles in the TV show "Doctor Who" - and published a paper on it in 2018.

It is a mind-bending idea that not only looks deep into the Earth's past but also far into its future, as humans change the climate swiftly and dramatically by burning fossil fuels.

"It is a thought experiment, but one that exposes our potential vulnerability globally," said Katharine Hayhoe, an atmospheric scientist at Texas Tech University, who was not involved in the research.

The Silurean hypothesis opens big questions about the trajectory of advanced civilisations and whether all those that harness energy on a global scale are destined to burn out, or whether there's a chance to live sustainably and survive for millions of years.

"These questions are all relevant to exactly the moment that we're in," said Frank. "We are pushing the planet into a new climate regime … we know this is true, right? And yet we're not doing anything about it."

The reason Schmidt had been mulling the possibility of previous advanced civilisations on Earth was an event deep in the past.

Around 55 million years ago, the planet's climate signals went haywire. Global temperatures spiked up to 15 degrees Fahrenheit and ecosystems collapsed, as huge amounts of planet-heating carbon were injected into the atmosphere.

This period, known as the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum and first noted in the 1990s, may have been the result of an enormous volcanic eruption, or maybe a sudden release of methane. But exactly why it happened is still something of a mystery.

What intrigued Schmidt were the similarities to what's happening now as humans push up temperatures and drive extinctions.

And it's not the only unexplained change deep in the planet's past that echoes our present, other periods have seen oceans starved of oxygen and sharp hikes in temperature.

The likelihood is these are natural climate events, but what if they weren't? How would we know? In their report, Frank and Schmidt go through the chain of possible evidence that might exist in support of a past advanced civilisation.

Today, only around one percent of the Earth's surface is urbanised - and it wouldn't take long for what we've built to be erased. The further back in time a hypothetical civilisation existed, the harder it would be to find direct evidence, like objects.

Over millions of years, the planet is resculpted as tectonic plates shift, volcanoes erupt and land erodes. The Earth's oldest large-scale stretch of land is the Negev Desert in southern Israel, at around 1.8 million years old.

Surface features may not provide much evidence, so the scientists looked at fossils. A vanishingly small fraction of animal species is fossilised, however, and even fewer are ever found. Dinosaurs roamed the Earth for about 180 million years, but only a few thousand near-complete fossils have been discovered.

It might be easy to miss a civilisation that only existed for 100,000 years - a mere blip in the 400-million-year-old history of complex life on the planet.

The researchers then considered traces left by chemical changes. Think of the Grand Canyon, Frank said, where you can see line after line representing different ages of the Earth.

"Every one of those strata is ground up rock that keeps a memory of what the chemistry of the Earth was like then." If a previous civilisation had altered the planet's chemistry - as humans have done by releasing vast amounts of carbon pollution - there might be a record.

The scientists also considered what other evidence humans might leave behind after our civilisation has ended, like the vast amounts of plastics as well as artificial hormones for agriculture and persistent chemicals, which do not break down in the environment. These might all show up in future sediments, many millions of years from now. As might the heavy metals used in electronics.

The point of the paper wasn't to establish whether the Silurian hypothesis is correct, Frank said. Instead, it was "to say here's the things you'd want to look for in a much more high-resolution way in order to see whether or not there was ever a civilisation before us."

Both Frank and Schmidt are in the strange position of having written a study about a theory neither believes in - they just say we cannot yet rule it out.

No one appears to have picked up the call for a deeper investigation in the years since, but some scientists have raised questions.

Jan Zalasiewicz, a geologist, paleontologist and emeritus professor at the University of Leicester in the UK, said the Silurian hypothesis is "wonderful and deeply thought-provoking idea."

But Schmidt and Frank underestimated just how much modern humans have transformed the planet, as well as "the effectiveness of the fossilisation process and how good it is at preserving a history of what has happened on our planet," he said.

We can't rule out intelligent pre-human societies, "dinosaurs that could sing complex arias, say, or Jurassic ammonites that could compose poetry," said Zalasiewicz, who co-wrote the 2025 book "Discarded: How Technofossils Will be Our Ultimate Legacy".

But as soon as cities are built, metals are smelted, plastics are made and discarded - these will leave a clear footprint, he said.

Zalasiewicz is comfortable ruling out the prior existence of the kind of advanced civilisation we live in today: "energy-guzzling, manipulative, constructional, and producing waste in colossal quantities."

And that's the beauty of science, Frank said. "You publish a paper, it's like, 'Woo, this is great,' and then somebody comes along and says you're wrong."

Someone else may find something that points in a different direction, and eventually, as research accumulates, a consensus will be formed.

For now, perhaps the most important reason to explore this hypothesis is the important questions it poses about the longevity of advanced technological civilisations like ours.

We're smart enough to develop technology, but we might not be smart enough to figure out how to deal with its climate-shifting consequences, Frank said.

"Are we an experiment that the planet has run, which is going to fail?"

title: OpenSlides – Open-source desktop app for animated code presentations
description: Free, open-source, offline desktop app for creating animated code presentations. Magic Move transitions, 16 syntax themes, highlight steps, autoplay , built with Tauri + Svelte5. An alternative to ...
fullText:
Beautiful code presentations for content creators, educators, and developers.

OpenSlides is a free, open-source, offline desktop app for turning code into polished slides with smooth, step-by-step transitions. It is a direct alternative to codeslides.app: create expressive code decks, keep your work on your own machine, and present without a subscription or internet connection.

Turn source code into presentation-ready slides. Move between code states with smooth Magic Move transitions, and build a visual story around your code instead of showing a static editor.

Reveal an idea line by line with stepped highlights. Control emphasis per step: dim amount, size-up scale, and custom transition timings — so you can guide viewers through a function, refactor, algorithm, or feature at a natural pace.

Choose light or dark presentation themes to match your style and recording setup.

Whether you are recording a tutorial, teaching a class, streaming a live build, giving a conference talk, or sharing a technical demo, OpenSlides helps you focus attention on the exact part of the code that matters.

Create a project, add your code to slides, then select the lines you want to explain. OpenSlides turns those selections into presentation steps, so you can guide viewers through a function, refactor, algorithm, or feature at a natural pace. When it is time to present, move through slides and highlight steps with the keyboard, use full-screen mode, or let the deck advance automatically.

Everything stays on your computer. That makes OpenSlides useful for private client work, offline classrooms, live events, and any workflow where you want your code and slides under your control.

Prebuilt installers for macOS, Windows, and Linux are available from the OpenSlides Releases page.

How a vectorless, Markdown personal LLM knowledge base became always-on and self-maintaining, then hardened against the agentic threat model: machine-enforced immutability, an append-only-log guard, the lethal trifecta cut by removing the exfiltration channel, least-privilege read-only librarian and write-scribe agents, and indirect-prompt-injection defenses.
