title: High winds could make fighting Spanish wildfires harder, officials say
description: MADRID, July 25 (Reuters) - Winds will pick up in Spain on Saturday, with gusts of up to 60 kph (38 mph), complicating the fight against out-of-control wildfires west of Madrid, the Interior Ministry
fullText:
MADRID, July 25 (Reuters) - Winds will pick up in Spain on Saturday, with gusts ‌of up to 60 kph (38 mph), ‌complicating the fight against out-of-control wildfires west of Madrid, the ​Interior Ministry warned.

Two separate wildfires in the Madrid region combined on Friday and became one huge blaze, but so far they have not merged ‌with another in ⁠Avila, in the neighbouring Castilla y Leon region.

The fires have so far ⁠forced more than 30,000 people to flee their homes in the Madrid region and more ​than 20,000 ​to be confined at ​home, the ministry ‌said on Saturday, in what officials have called the region's worst fire on record.

Overnight weather conditions had helped the firefighters.

"The change in weather conditions (less wind, higher humidity, and lower temperature) has ‌greatly benefited the fight against ​the forest fires, which have ​advanced little ​and decreased in intensity," the central ‌government in Madrid said on ​Saturday morning.

Plumes ​of thick smoke could be seen in the sky west of the capital.

More than ​9,000 hectares ‌have burned in the wildfires in the ​Madrid region, authorities said.

title: Wildfires in France drive 250,000 people from their homes, creep toward wine city
description: LEGE-CAP FERRET, France (AP) — A raging wildfire in southwest France forced the evacuation of 55,000 people overnight Sunday, taking the total forced out of their homes to 220,000 in one region alone ...
fullText:
LEGE-CAP FERRET, France (AP) — A raging wildfire in southwest France forced the evacuation of 55,000 people overnight Sunday, taking the total forced out of their homes to 220,000 in one region alone as the flames have crept ever closer to the wine region city of Bordeaux.

Authorities in the Gironde region, where Bordeaux is located, issued overnight evacuation orders for five more localities southwest of the historic city.

Gusting winds fed the flames overnight, accelerating the spread of the fire that has been burning out of control since midweek, the authorities' statement said.

The Gironde prefect also ordered the partial closure of a major highway heading southwest from Bordeaux.

The city's mayor said the fire "is still at the gates of the metropolitan area," having advanced to about 15 kilometers (9 miles) from Bordeaux at its closest point.

A second fire burning further south in the Landes region has also forced the evacuation of 30,000 people this week, taking the total driven out of their homes by the blazes to more than 250,000.

In neighboring Spain, authorities have evacuated 70,000 people this week because of fires west of Madrid.

title: How Abhijeet Dipke became the face of India's first Gen Z protest movement, and won
description: They were just six words posted on X in a moment of frustration:  "What if all cockroaches come together?"
fullText:
NEW DELHI, July 25 (Reuters) - They were just six words posted on X in a moment of frustration:

"What if all cockroaches come together?"

Now, its 30-year-old author, Abhijeet Dipke, is the face of what is arguably India's biggest street protest against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government ‌since he took office in 2014.

The political communications strategist's post, sent on May 16, was initially a witty response to comments by Supreme Court judge ‌Surya Kant, likening India's unemployed youth in a speech to "cockroaches".

Kant later said his comments were misconstrued.

A satirical platform called the "Cockroach Janta Party" (CJP) had sprung up, providing a rallying point ​for millions of young Indians frustrated over high unemployment and exam paper leaks and seeking greater government accountability.

Over the past week, tens of thousands gathered in New Delhi demanding the resignation of Indian Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over leaks of the medical entrance test paper that affected some 2 million students in May and have been linked to several student suicides. Pradhan resigned on Saturday: a major victory for the young protesters and one of Modi's biggest defeats.

Protests were reported in other parts of the country too, including the financial ‌hub of Mumbai.

At the centre of it all is Dipke.

Based in the U.S. city of Boston until early June, he flew back to India to launch a protest near the Jantar Mantar observatory in the heart of Delhi.

Since then — and particularly after a police crackdown on demonstrators on Monday sparked public outrage — ⁠he has become a constant presence on a raised platform at the protest site.

Bearded and dressed in a T-shirt and jeans, Dipke addresses crowds of hundreds, urging them to remain peaceful while maintaining pressure on the government.

Even if the CJP has several organisers, Dipke has become its most recognisable face, drawing both admiration and criticism.

Dipke was born in Aurangabad in the western Indian ​state ​of Maharashtra into a Dalit family, one of India's most historically disadvantaged communities.

"My father comes from ​a very humble background. He grew up in extreme poverty. My ‌grandfather was just a farmer," Dipke told Reuters in May.

His Dalit identity has long shaped his politics.

When he arrived in Delhi on June 6, Dipke held aloft a copy of "My Autobiography" by B.R. Ambedkar, a champion of Dalit rights and key architect of India's democratic constitution, as supporters and security personnel swarmed around him.

In 2020, Dipke joined the social media team of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), where he said he developed a style of political messaging built around memes, humour and satire.

He is no longer associated with the party, though AAP and several other Indian opposition parties have backed the movement.

In 2023, Dipke moved to the United States to pursue a master's degree in ‌public relations in Boston, but continued to follow Indian politics closely.

FROM A SOCIAL MEDIA POST TO ​A MOVEMENT

Dipke says he is still trying to process his prominence.

One of the first people to amplify ​the movement was Delhi-based YouTuber Meghnad S. Soon after Dipke's post, he and ​a friend used AI tools to build a satirical website announcing the formation of the Cockroach Janta Party.

"I saw the page and ‌thought it was damn hilarious," Meghnad said.

The Instagram account amassed 22 ​million followers in a matter of days ​before swelling further to 25 million recently.

"That's how organic it was," Meghnad said.

But as the online movement grew, so did the stakes.

Speaking to Reuters from Boston in May, Dipke said:

"This is a movement to change the political discourse of India. The youth of India has largely vanished from the mainstream political discourse."

Despite threats ​to himself and his family, Dipke decided to return to ‌India. He has said he will stay at least until the students get justice.

Since June 6, Dipke has remained at the protest site as ​the demonstrations have swelled and can frequently be seen appealing to protesters to keep the movement peaceful, speaking to the media or grabbing brief ​naps.

title: Gomez injury overshadows winning start for Iraola
description: Liverpool start life under Andoni Iraola with a 4-2 win over Sunderland thanks to goals from Kieran Morrison, Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas.
fullText:
Liverpool started life under Andoni Iraola with a 4-2 win over Sunderland thanks to goals from Kieran Morrison, Dominik Szoboszlai, Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas.

But the Iraola era had initially got off to the worst possible start when Joe Gomez, who started the game as centre-back and captain, went down injured and was taken off in the eighth minute.

"Probably the worst news has been straight away the injury of Joe. We were happy because we were going through training without losing any players and unluckily for us we've lost Joe straight away," said Iraola, who was also without new signing Jeremy Jacquet - who plays centre-half - for the opening friendly of Liverpool's tour of the USA.

"With Jeremy we decided to take it easy with him. He's had a lot of months without playing and he's been training very well but we're going to take it easy with him," Iraola added. "He will play probably in the last game of this tour and he will have time to have minutes."

With Virgil van Dijk given extra time off following the Netherlands' World Cup campaign, it meant that two teenage centre-backs held the line until the 68th minute.

Mor Talla N'diaye, 18, and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, made their debuts and both performed admirably given the situation but neither can be expected to feature regularly yet. Meanwhile, Giovanni Leoni, 19, is still undergoing individual training as he works his way back from a severe ACL tear.

Iraola said earlier in the week that his squad was "very thin" defensively. Liverpool's sporting director, Richard Hughes, was in Nashville for the game and if he wasn't aware already, seeing Gomez trudge off must have underlined how they are desperately short when it comes to experience in the centre-back department.

On Friday evening, some of the Liverpool squad took the short walk from their hotel in downtown Nashville to Broadway - the famous entertainment district here in the state of Tennessee.

Szoboszlai, who was among that group, certainly took some inspiration. Wearing the armband after coming on at half-time and picking up from exactly where he left off last season, the Hungarian scored a belter from outside the box to level the game at 2-2 after Sunderland had gone ahead through Timur Tutierov, having initially levelled through Enzo le Fee.

Seeing Harvey Elliott make a surging run on his first game back at the club, after his spell at Aston Villa, to assist Morrison for Liverpool's opener was another positive. Morrison showed his quality with a lovely left-footed finish after cutting in from the right.

The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international was brilliant all evening and asked plenty of questions of the Sunderland backline. Liverpool still need a quality winger after losing Mohamed Salah but Morrison showed why he could be an option off the bench if he doesn't go out on loan this summer.

Iraola was constantly out of his seat in the dugout and his side pressed well in phases but the manner in which they conceded both goals shows there is still plenty to be done. Le Fee was given the freedom of Nashville to fire his strike past Giorgi Mamardashvili and Liverpool were opened up far too easy for Tutierov's goal.

For the 24,897 fans inside, who were primarily following Liverpool, it provided great joy to see fan favourite Chiesa make it 3-2, with a brilliant finish after a good ball from Calvin Ramsay, before Koumas capped off an impressive display with a goal to wrap up the game.

Earlier on in that move, Josh Abe played an important role carrying the ball up the pitch down the right flank. Abe only turned 16 last week and came on for his Liverpool debut in the second half. The England youth international is a highly rated prospect and there were glimpses here of why.

Iraola and co head back to their base in Chicago with a win under their belt but well aware that this is just the start. Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch have already arrived in the Windy City and start training on Sunday.

"It doesn't matter the result but keep pushing, don't relax, get used to not playing too comfortable. We still have a lot of things to improve," the Liverpool head coach said.

His side are next in action against Wrexham in New York on Thursday (00.30 BST). Sunderland face Leeds at the Sports Illustrated Stadium in New Jersey at the same time.

title: A Hims cofounder fired his entire marketing team for AI. Now his 24/7 online vet service is growing 20% a month
description: Joe Spector helped build a multibillion-dollar telehealth company. Now he’s on to own remote vet services.
fullText:
When Joe Spector's corgi, Eddie, ate four M&Ms, the Hims cofounder spent hours trying to find an emergency vet who could see him. One office pointed him to a pet poison hotline, and another was an hour away and had a four-hour wait. The bill came out to $2,000.

Spector thought at the time "this does not have to be that way," he told Fortune.

That stressful scramble in 2021 sparked the idea for Dutch, the veterinary telehealth company Spector launched on July 1 of that year after helping build and take public Hims & Hers, the direct-to-consumer telehealth brand best known for treating hair loss and sexual wellness. Those companies have since grown exponentially to cover an array of health concerns.

Dutch, which just marked its fifth anniversary, offers members video visits with veterinarians for a flat $100 a year covering up to five pets. That amounts to roughly the cost of a single in-person visit at a regular veterinary office. The company now operates in 35 states, up from eight at launch, as more states loosen restrictions on veterinary telemedicine. The company has logged millions of interactions and now counts more than 100,000 active members, according to the company. Dutch raised $20 million in early 2022 to scale the platform, in a round led by Forerunner Ventures.

The company declined to share its current revenue and valuation, but its revenue grew 5.5x between 2022 and 2023, 2.2x between 2023 and 2024, and 1.8x between 2024 and 2025.

Although Dutch is clearly charting its growth path now, it was a bit stagnant for a while. Now Spector is making a bigger bet on how the company markets itself.

Late last year, Spector said, Dutch was paying an outside agency roughly $50,000 a month to produce five pieces of creative material, or about $10,000 apiece.

"It's both expensive and it's just limited because so much of marketing, especially with a new product, is just testing to see what's resonating," Spector said.

So he fired that agency. That drastic move is somewhat reminiscent of Bolt's CEO telling Fortune at its Workplace Innovation Summit in May he had ditched his entire human resources team, although the executives had very different motivations for their moves.

In its place is a new in-house marketing team leaning heavily on AI tools to generate content, from static ads to full animated and live-action commercials. Now Dutch produces about 50 pieces of content a month internally, or a 10x jump, Spector said. That's enough work to cost roughly half a million dollars a month through an agency, he said. Just as important as the savings, he said, is the ability to test what actually lands with pet owners who often don't know virtual vet care exists.

Free Agents the Saints Could Bring In for Training Camp
description: Some moves could still be made.
fullText:
The New Orleans Saints had an extremely busy offseason with the goal of getting this team to another level in 2026. Strides were made last season, but it was clear upgrades had to be made, and the Saints got that done. It was not a perfect offseason; that was always going to be impossible given how many roster spots needed attention, but it was impressive. The entire offense has been reworked to the point that there's no real clear hole on that side of the ball. For QB Tyler Shough, these upgrades are going to be significant for his development. On defense, there's a good chance this group becomes the priority next offseason.

Still, becoming patient after the offseason the Saints had could spell trouble because you never know what injuries will happen or what position groups end up being worse than expected. This happens every offseason for every team. Trying to find potential upgrades or great depth pieces in free agency can go a long way this season, and here are some potential names for the Saints.

First is a similar move to what the Saints made last season, but this time a signing. Kind of randomly, New Orleans made a trade for center Luke Fortner during the preseason. The move made sense with Erik McCoy's injury history, and it ended up being a really important trade. McCoy did indeed go down with an injury, and Fortner had to step in for most of the season. He ended up being a solid starter for the Saints, which did lead to him getting a decent contract in free agency.

Just like last year, the Saints need to find a solid backup center just in case another McCoy injury occurs, and although that player could be on the roster, competition is important. One player that sticks out is former Chicago Bears center Ryan Bates. When he was on the Bills, Bates was a decent depth piece, but injuries in Chicago completely derailed any impact he would have made. This could make him a very cheap option for a team needing center depth, and that's where the Saints could strike.

The other player that could make a lot of sense for the Saints is former New York Giants LB Bobby Okereke. LB is such an interesting position for the Saints because of the departure of Demario Davis. Kaden Elliss was a great signing, but his attention may be split because of Brandon Staley's potential utilization of him at OLB.

LB depth will be extremely important for the Saints, and if last season showed us anything, the players on the roster may not be ready to make it happen. That thought could change quickly in training camp and the preseason, but if not, Okereke should be a target.

title: Brian Windhorst Joins Zach Lowe in Sounding Alarm Over Trail Blazers’ Future
description: Stalled arena negotiations and escalating rhetoric between ownership and city officials have sparked relocation fears, potentially triggering an all-out war for the franchise’s future in Portland.
fullText:
The Portland Trail Blazers' increasingly contentious arena negotiations have caught the attention of another prominent NBA voice.

And Brian Windhorst's warning may be the strongest yet.

Days after Zach Lowe urged the NBA to prevent Portland from losing its franchise, Windhorst acknowledged that the possibility of relocation is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore as negotiations surrounding the Moda Center deteriorate.

"It's getting worse by the day," Windhorst said on ESPN. "The rhetoric between the politicians and the Trail Blazers is deteriorating."

Windhorst then turned his attention toward Monday's meeting of the Blazers' board of directors.

Although he acknowledged he doesn't know what will emerge from the meeting, he suggested ownership could respond aggressively to the city's proposed term sheet.

"It could be a declaration of all-out war," Windhorst said.

That's ... quite the escalation.

The city wants the Blazers to commit to a new long-term lease before public funding is released for the proposed Moda Center renovation.

Ownership, however, reportedly considers several provisions within Portland's initial proposal to be non-starters, including annual payments in lieu of property taxes, requirements involving union labor and additional community benefits.

Windhorst highlighted two recent comments from anonymous team officials that demonstrate just how far apart the sides have become.

"Why would the city send this knowing we aren't going to sign it?" one official said, according to The Oregonian/OregonLive.

Another delivered an even more pointed message.

"The city of Portland doesn't even recognize they have a sweetheart deal," the official said. "If they don't want us, then that's fine."

Those comments help explain why the conversation has expanded far beyond Portland.

Lowe recently warned that the NBA couldn't allow ownership to "hijack" the franchise and remove it from one of the league's most passionate basketball markets.

Now, Windhorst is openly discussing the possibility of ownership's next move becoming a declaration of war against the city.

Neither analyst reported that relocation is imminent.

The Blazers' current lease runs through 2030, while the organization continues to insist that its preferred outcome remains renovating the Moda Center and securing a long-term future in Portland.

But the tone surrounding those negotiations has undeniably changed.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver acknowledged the talks had gone "off track." Team officials have discussed abandoning the current framework, argued relocation could make financial sense and repeatedly criticized the city's proposal.

Monday's board meeting could reveal whether ownership still intends to negotiate within the current structure or plans to reset the process entirely.

What began as a dispute over public funding has now prompted two of the NBA's most recognizable media figures to publicly question the Blazers' future.

At this point, that concern is becoming as difficult to dismiss as the possibility they're warning about.

title: Minnesota Vikings Draw Bold Trade Prediction for 2026 Season
description: With Sam Darnold thriving, analysts project a shocking divorce between Minnesota and J.J. McCarthy, potentially reuniting the young quarterback with a former Michigan coach in Baltimore.
fullText:
Trade predictions are aplenty for the Minnesota Vikings as we turn toward preseason in the National Football League. The Vikings' status as a viable playoff contender incentivises them to make the most of their current standing and get even better.

We have seen some of the wilder trade proposals. Justin Jefferson has commanded buzz to reel in two first round picks in exchange for a trade. But we feel pretty confident the Vikings would say no even to that kind of trade. Jefferson means too much to the organization.

A new trade proposal has emerged. In no surprise, NFL analysts are looking at the possibility that the Vikings trade one of their two well-known quarterbacks in Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy. One analyst says it's McCarthy that could head to another team.

SB Nation's Jarrett Bailey predicts that the Vikings could trade former Michigan Wolverines quarterback J.J. McCarthy to the Ravens to join up with his old team's former defensive coordinator Jesse Minter. Here's what Bailey wrote on the topic.

"The writing is on the wall for J.J. McCarthy. The Vikings won 14 games with Sam Darnold, didn’t bring him back, and then watched him win a Super Bowl while they limped to a 9-8 record. McCarthy completed less than 60 percent of his passes with 11 touchdowns to 12 interceptions. He gets dealt to Baltimore and Jesse Minter, who won a National Championship with McCarthy at Michigan as the Wolverines’ defensive coordinator."

It's unclear how close McCarthy and Minter are after their time with the Wolverines, but we do know that they were a good combination in Ann Arbor. Minter's defense suffocated any offense from opposition, while McCarthy consistently dominated third downs with clutch conversions all season long in his final college campaign.

McCarthy has not put up crazy numbers in college or the pros, but he certainly had the penchant for clutch play in Michigan. If one good trait translated to the NFL, it's that. McCarthy proved to be significantly better in the fourth quarter for the Vikings than the first three. Perhaps Minter's system would be a better fit for McCarthy in his current level, though he is working to improve this offseason.

It's no guarantee that the Ravens would make such trade for McCarthy as Bailey suggests. Included in the rest of his suggestions is a Dallas Cowboys Super Bowl win over the Cincinnati Bengals. If quarterback Dak Prescott's track record or the Cowboys' last 30 years of football are of is any indication, that's probably not going to happen.

Even so, it's possible that the Vikings trade McCarthy to another team. We'll update any trade news as it comes.

title: Yankees Give Dire Sign on Ryan McMahon After Trade Speculation
description: The New York Yankees have benched struggling third baseman Ryan McMahon for two games in a row. The post Yankees Give Dire Sign on Ryan McMahon After Trade Speculation appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Yankees have been urged to move on from struggling third baseman Ryan McMahon, and the team could be getting an early glimpse of what it looks like without him in the lineup.

The team took McMahon out of the starting lineup for the first two games of their weekend set against the Philadelphia Phillies, the first time since April that he’s hit the bench for back-to-back games. The Yankees announced that veteran Amed Rosario would instead take third base and bat leadoff, leaving McMahon with an uncertain future as the trade deadline approaches.

The Yankees have not given further details on why McMahon has been sent to the bench against the Phillies, though he was healthy enough to come in as a defensive replacement for Rosario in the seventh inning of Friday’s 1-0 win over the Phillies.

McMahon also registered an at-bat in the top of the ninth inning, reaching first after being hit by pitch. He was solid in the field, recording a defensive assist in the eighth inning afte throwing out Alec Bohm.

But McMahon has struggled this season, leading to some speculation that the team could part ways with him before the upcoming MLB trade deadline. Reporter Devon Platana of SI.com suggested that the Yankees should “do whatever it takes to move on from McMahon and upgrade 3B, as he’s due to make another $16 million next season before becoming a free agent.” Platana noted that the Yankees would likely lose him for nothing in 2027, so the team should try to squeeze out whatever return they can manage this year.

While McMahon’s future with the Yankees could be murky, another infielder appears to be on his way out of the lineup. Shortstop prospect George Lombard Jr. is on the fast track to the Bronx this season, with reporter Jon Heyman noting that he should be with the team in a matter of weeks.

“Shortstop isn’t a top priority, partly due to faith in prospect George Lombard Jr., a terrific defender,” Heyman noted in the New York Post. “Recent estimates suggest Lombard could be up in about two weeks.”

That could mean the end of the line for Anthony Volpe, who like McMahon has struggled. SI.com reporter Joseph Randazzo noted that the team will likely keep shortstop Jose Caballero as a partner for Lombard, and could look to trade Volpe.

“While Caballero should still have a job on the Yankees as a roving infielder and outfielder, which is what he was for most of his career with the Tampa Bay Rays before coming to New York, it’s Volpe who should be the most concerned,” Randazzo wrote. “For one, Volpe only plays shortstop. He doesn’t have the versatility that Caballero has.”

Randazzo added that Volpe’s options with the team will grow more limited once Lombard arrives.

“Right now, the only options for Volpe are being traded or sent down to Triple-A,” Randazzo wrote. “If he wants to start, that would only happen if Lombard got hurt or they dealt him.”

title: Davante Adams addresses Rams nearly trading him for first time
description: The Rams nearly traded Davante Adams for A.J. Brown before deciding against it, and the veteran wideout addressed those talks for the first time.
fullText:
During the 2026 NFL offseason, the Los Angeles Rams explored potential moves to add star wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles. In the midst of those talks, reports came out that the Rams considered trading Davante Adams in order to add Brown, which head coach Sean McVay later confirmed.

The move never materialized, and Brown would eventually be traded to the New England Patriots. If circumstances were different, there's a good chance Adams could've departed one year after joining the team.

Adams was asked by reporters on Saturday about those rumors, choosing to take the professional high road and avoid making those talks a personal gripe.

"I'm a teenager in this league now, so, I mean, you got to understand there's certain things that each team, you know, does or has to do in order to -- just from top to bottom -- it's just the way that this business goes," stated Adams.

Rams WR Davante Adams on the offseason trade rumors:

"I'm a teenager in this league now, so, I mean, you got to understand there's certain things that each team, you know, does or has to do in order to -- just from top to bottom -- it's just the way that this business goes." pic.twitter.com/YukgMbPLrP

— Benjamin Royer (@thebenroyer) July 25, 2026

While Adams would be more than justified in being angry, especially after leading the NFL in receiving touchdowns and helping Matthew Stafford win MVP, his decision to focus on the things he can control is why he remains a top player, despite his veteran status. Adams also expressed that he's happy to be back and is ready to get to work.

It's easy to see why so many within the organization hold Adams in such high regard, despite 2026 being only his second year with the franchise. Adams is entering the final year of his deal.

title: A Dozen And A Half Decisive ‘Dawgs: #15 Khalil Barnes
description: When Georgia landed Khalil Barnes out of the transfer portal in January it marked a full-circle moment for the Bogart, native. Barnes grew up minutes from Athens, starred at North Oconee High School, but chose Clemson over the hometown Bulldogs coming out of high school. But three seasons and 30 starts later, he is finally […]
fullText:
When Georgia landed Khalil Barnes out of the transfer portal in January it marked a full-circle moment for the Bogart, native. Barnes grew up minutes from Athens, starred at North Oconee High School, but chose Clemson over the hometown Bulldogs coming out of high school. But three seasons and 30 starts later, he is finally putting on the red and black, arriving with one year of eligibility remaining and skills that should make him an immediate factor in Kirby Smart’s defense.

Barnes’ body of work at Clemson is substantial. Over three seasons, he racked up 139 total tackles, 7 interceptions, 11 pass breakups, 6.5 tackles for loss, 3 forced fumbles, and a sack. He burst onto the scene as a true freshman in 2022, becoming the first player of the Dabo Swinney era to record multiple interceptions and multiple forced fumbles in his debut season, earning Freshman All-America recognition.

Barnes’ best all-around year with the Country Gentlemen came in 2024, when he posted 61 tackles and 4 interceptions, third highest in the ACC, while helping Clemson reach the College Football Playoff. His 2025 season was more quiet. Nagging injuries limited him to 10 games and 9 starts, and he finished with 40 tackles, 5 quarterback hurries, 2 pass breakups, and one tackle for loss, and without an interception for the first time in his career.

Barnes brings Power 4 experience, football IQ, and versatility to a secondary that lost five players in the transfer portal this offseason. Coach Smart praised him as intelligent, well-coached, and comfortable having played multiple positions and defensive schemes at a high level. Barnes’ 2022 and 2024 tape shows a player with natural ball skills and the instincts to be around the football, evidenced by his takeaway numbers early in his career. At 6’0 and 200 pounds he also brings physicality against the run, reflected in his tackle for loss production.

The questions surrounding Barnes are tied mostly to his 2025 season. The lack of turnovers and reduced role, driven largely by injury, leave some uncertainty about whether his playmaking ability will translate immediately to the SEC.

Barnes appears ticketed to start at the STAR position where Georgia has had success plugging in transfer standouts in the past. Tykee Smith for example earned All-SEC honors in 2023 after transferring in from West Virginia and taking over that slot. With former five star prospect Joenel Aguero transferring out, Barnes and sophomore Rasean Dinkins will likely be the competitors for the STAR spot in fall camp. But Barnes, with his experience and physical tools, could be a key component if the Bulldog secondary is to live up to its substantial potential.

In this age of college football coaches don’t take transfers, especially transfers like Barnes with one year of eligibility, unless they expect that guy to make an immediate impact. A successful season for Khalil Barnes would involve a return to his 2024 form, with solid production and an injury-free season. It will also be interesting to see how much of a leadership Barnes can assume as a “brand new veteran” on a defense that returns experienced starters at every level.

Spire Motorsports will have a powerful presence at the front of the field for tomorrow’s Brickyard 400, as all three of the organization’s entries qualified inside the top six at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

Carson Hocevar led the way in a dominant qualifying performance, securing third career pole postion with a lap of 48.232 seconds. The result gives Spire Motorsports its best possible starting spot heading into one of NASCAR’s biggest races of the season.

Daniel Suarez followed closely behind, qualifying second with a time of 48.288 seconds. Suarez missed the pole by just 0.056 seconds. Michael McDowell completed an impressive qualifying day for the organization by securing sixth place with a lap of 48.449 seconds. McDowell was just 0.217 seconds behind Hocevar’s pole-winning time.

With Hocevar starting from the pole, Suarez alongside him and McDowell lurking in sixth, Spire Motorsports will have three cars positioned to make an immediate impact in the Brickyard 400.

The top five will feature Hocevar, Suarez, Tyler Reddick, Ty Gibbs and Denny Hamlin, while McDowell will start sixth. Corey Heim, Alex Bowman, AJ Allmendinger and Kyle Larson rounded out the top 10.

title: Cathy Engelbert Condemns Online Abuse Directed at WNBA Players
description: Cathy Engelbert opened her All-Star press conference by condemning the racism, misogyny, and homophobia directed at WNBA players, days after meeting with the union.
fullText:
Cathy Engelbert opened her annual midseason press conference Saturday in Chicago by addressing player safety and online abuse, and she condemned the racism, misogyny, and homophobia directed at WNBA players.

Engelbert referenced the meeting she held with players earlier in the week. The press conference came hours before tip-off of the All-Star Game at the United Center.

Engelbert and leadership from the WNBPA met by video Tuesday night at the union's request. The call included the union's executive committee and its Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion Committee. The league and the union released a joint statement Wednesday describing the conversation as being about the recent increase in racist, hateful, and abusive messages directed at players. The league committed in that statement to continuing to enhance security resources and to working with the union on collaborations with outside organizations. The two sides said Tuesday's meeting is expected to be the first of several.

Engelbert also said Saturday that communication with players can be better across the board, and that preferred modes of communication can create a disconnect.

Phoenix forward Alyssa Thomas called on the league and on Engelbert to act after she received death threats and abusive messages online. Thomas was suspended one game for making contact with the throat of Indiana guard Caitlin Clark during the Mercury's 111-109 win over the Fever on June 24. No foul was called on the floor, and the league later upgraded the play to a Flagrant 2. Thomas said on June 30 that she had not heard from the league about the suspension or about the threats.

Chelsea Gray posted a message she received from a man that included a racial slur. The man was identified and lost his job at Hilton Grand Vacations.

Natasha Cloud, who has said previously that Engelbert has not done enough for players, said Tuesday that there is a limit to what the league can do about people who choose to be hateful.

WNBPA president Nneka Ogwumike met with Engelbert earlier in the week. Ogwumike has been union president since 2016.

The collective bargaining agreement ratified in March requires larger team medical staffs, including two athletic trainers, two team physicians, a strength and conditioning coach, a physical therapist, a massage therapist, and access to a nutritionist. The league and the WNBPA reached a verbal agreement on the deal March 18. Players approved it March 23, and the Board of Governors ratified it March 24.

Engelbert announced at Saturday's press conference that the league will open centralized Replay Center operations at the start of the 2027 season.

This is the WNBA's 30th season. The league expanded from 13 to 15 teams in May with the additions of the Portland Fire and the Toronto Tempo.

Former president Barack Obama spoke with the All-Stars on Friday at the Obama Presidential Center on the South Side of Chicago, where the teams practiced. Engelbert and Chicago civic leaders spoke before he arrived.

The All-Star Game tips off at 8:30 p.m. ET on ABC. The 2026 regular season runs through Sept. 24.

title: Former Leicester City striker Patson Daka shines in Hamburg debut
description: Patson Daka required only 28 minutes of action to make a major impression on his Hamburg debut. The 27-year-old directly contributed to all three goals as Hamburg concluded their Austrian training cam...
fullText:
Patson Daka required only 28 minutes of action to make a major impression on his Hamburg debut. The 27-year-old directly contributed to all three goals as Hamburg concluded their Austrian training camp with a 3-1 friendly victory over 1. FC Heidenheim.

Daka replaced Yussuf Poulsen in the 34th minute and immediately won the penalty from which Albert Grønbæk opened the scoring. Shortly after half-time, the Zambian international supplied Rayan Philippe for Hamburg’s second before scoring the third himself.

The former Leicester City striker was then withdrawn as planned following only three days of team training.

“It’s nice to see how Patson is contributing,” HSV head coach Merlin Polzin – as quoted by Kicker – remarked afterwards. “The connection among the players is always very important to me. That connection can’t be fully established in such a short time, but he’s full of life and very communicative.”

As noted in previous Get German Football News coverage, Daka arrived in Hamburg determined to put several difficult seasons behind him. The former Red Bull Salzburg attacker also expressed his desire to remain with HSV beyond the initial term of his contract.

“I’m never afraid of the future,” Daka said at his official introductory press event. “I trust God, and my present is the future because tomorrow is not guaranteed. What I do today determines what will happen to me tomorrow. When I experience a difficult moment, I do something about it.”

“My desire is to remain here for as long as possible,” Daka continued. “Everything is possible. I want to help the group quickly.”

Three days of training and 28 highly productive minutes suggest that Daka has already begun fulfilling that wish.

title: Bayern Munich among top five clubs to be compensated by FIFA following World Cup
description: A lot of risk, less reward?
fullText:
The relationship between club and international football has always been shaky at best. Clubs fear injuries that could derail an entire season while international teams pine for their nation’s top talents — a complex conflict of interest.

Nowhere is the conflict as prominent as the FIFA World Cup. Clubs have no choice but to surrender their talent to their national teams. The hesitancy isn’t a product of not wanting players to represent their countries on the world’s greatest stage. It is rather a matter of risk.

Already fatigued after a long season of club football, players are at a heightened risk of injury — not to mention the select few who decide to play through afflictions for the pride of representing their country at the World Cup. Germany’s Lennart Karl and Nico Schlotterbeck suffered tournament-ending injuries, while Belgium’s Amadou Onana sustained a torn ACL mid-tournament. Argentinian pair Facundo Medina and Lisandro Martínez both face an extended stint on the sidelines, England’s Tino Livramento picked up a fresh setback in a long line of past injuries, and Morocco’s Abde Ezzalzouli was ruled out for six weeks after injuring his knee.

Among other reasons, to make up for the immense risk FIFA offers compensation for clubs whose players feature at the World Cup.

According to Kicker (via @iMiaSanMia), Bayern Munich is one of the clubs that will benefit the most.

Compensation payments paid out by FIFA to clubs for releasing their players for the World Cup:

1- Manchester City €3.08m
2- PSG €2.49m
3- Arsenal €2.42m
4- Bayern €2.3m
5- Barcelona €2.2m
6- Chelsea €2.12m

Whether the compensation provided by FIFA truly outweighs the extra kilometres players clock and a heightened risk of injury is up for debate. But, the fact that there is compensation — a luxury that didn’t always exist — is a step in the right direction.

title: Giants bury Angels early, cruise to lopsided win
description: Robbie Ray silenced the Angels' bats, and Rafael Devers made sure the rest didn't matter.
fullText:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Angels never had a chance to make this one interesting.

San Francisco jumped on Ryan Johnson early, scoring nine runs over the first four innings and putting the game away well before the seventh-inning stretch, cruising to a 9-2 win over Los Angeles at Oracle Park on Saturday.

Johnson didn't make it out of the fourth. The right-hander was tagged for eight runs on eight hits in 3 1/3 innings, and the Giants' third-inning uprising did the real damage. Jung Hoo Lee blew it open with a two-out, three-run homer, to make it 5-0. Logan O'Hoppe tried to salvage something out of the frame with an ABS challenge on a strikeout call, but the review only confirmed the Angels were out of the inning.

Jul 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; San Francisco Giants right fielder Jung Hoo Lee (51) hits a three run RBI home run against the Los Angeles Angels during the third inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images

San Francisco wasn't finished. Devers added a three-run homer, his 22nd, in the fourth to push the lead to 9-0 and chase Johnson from the game for good. Brent Suter and Kirby Yates combined to keep the Angels quiet in relief, and by the time Los Angeles got the ball back to its lineup, the game had already been decided.

Jul 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; San Francisco Giants first baseman Rafael Devers (16) celebrates with second baseman Luis Arraez (1) after batting him in on a three run home run against the Los Angeles Angels during the fourth inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images

Robbie Ray made sure of that. The right-hander cruised through six innings without allowing an earned run, scattering six hits and striking out five to improve to 9-6 on the season. Los Angeles didn't get a runner past second base against him.

The Angels didn't get on the board until the seventh, and even that took some work. Jose Siri walked, moved into scoring position on a Logan O'Hoppe single and a Zach Neto hit-by-pitch, and scored on a Mike Trout double play before Vaughn Grissom flew out to end the inning.

Jul 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Angels shortstop Zach Neto (9) reacts after being hit by pitch against the San Francisco Giants during the seventh inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images

Things only got more lopsided from there. With the bullpen thin from the blowout, Los Angeles turned to catcher Tyler Heineman to pitch the eighth inning, and he retired the side in order. The Angels tacked on one more run in the ninth on a Vaughn Grissom walk that scored Siri, but it did little to change the final margin.

Jul 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Angels left fielder Jose Siri (28) is walked in after San Francisco Giants starting pitcher Keaton Winn (67) threw four balls for a walk with bases loaded during the ninth inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images

Devers finished 3-for-4 with four RBIs, and Jung Hoo Lee added two hits and three RBIs of his own as San Francisco piled up 11 hits and got length from Ray at the top of the rotation. Siri had two hits and scored twice for the Angels.

Los Angeles will look to salvage the series finale Sunday, when Jose Soriano takes the mound against Carson Whisenhunt, with first pitch scheduled for 1:05 p.m. PT at Oracle Park.

title: Dodgers to activate closer Edwin Díaz from IL on Wednesday after 3 months out
description: Veteran utility man Kiké Hernández will also reportedly be activated on Tuesday.
fullText:
Edwin Díaz, the most expensive closer in baseball, is about to return to the Los Angeles Dodgers. With hopefully better results this time.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Saturday the team plans to activate Díaz on Wednesday, according to AM 570's Dave Vassegh. Veteran utility man Kiké Hernández will also reportedly be activated on Tuesday.

Díaz is currently on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City and is scheduled to make one more appearance on Sunday.

Díaz joined the Dodgers on a three-year, $69 million contract in free agency last winter, making him MLB's highest-paid reliever after a standout career with the New York Mets. The early returns were less than what the Dodgers would have hoped, with seven earned runs allowed in his first six innings.

At 32 years old, Díaz struggled with his control, which wasn't above average even in the best of times. After seven appearances, the Dodgers shelved him in April due to loose bodies in his elbow.

Since then, the Dodgers have leaned on a resurgent Tanner Scott as their closer, an ironic development given they only signed Díaz after Scott's struggles in his first season on a similarly large contract. Overall, the team's bullpen ranks seventh in MLB with a 3.77 ERA.

Díaz and Hernández are two of several names the Dodgers will be hoping to re-introduce in the second half, with starting pitchers Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, reliever Blake Treinen and catcher Will Smith among those waiting in the wings.

title: Patriots Land ‘Fluid, Fast’ Ex-Alabama Wide Receiver as Training Camp Opens
description: The Patriots added a “fluid, fast” former Alabama wide receiver as New England opens training camp and evaluates its revamped receiving corps. The post Patriots Land ‘Fluid, Fast’ Ex-Alabama Wide Receiver as Training Camp Opens appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New England Patriots didn’t wait long to pounce on a wide receiver the Carolina Panthers had just cut loose. New England claimed Kobe Prentice off waivers on Saturday, adding a speedy, undrafted rookie who lasted barely a day on Carolina’s roster before the Patriots scooped him up, according to reporter Aaron Wilson. To create the roster spot, New England released offensive lineman Sebastian Gutierrez, according to ESPN’s Mike Reiss.

The Patriots also held their first public practice of 2026 training camp on Saturday.

Carolina had waived Prentice a day earlier to clear space after claiming offensive tackle Ryan Hayes off waivers from the Tennessee Titans, ending Prentice’s brief run with the Panthers pretty much before it began. He’d signed with Carolina in early May after going undrafted, and worked through spring practices and the first stretch of training camp before becoming a roster casualty.

Receiver Kobe Prentice in his time with the Alabama Crimson Tide.

Calera, Alabama, produced Prentice as a track sprinter turned football star, and the dual-threat background shows up on tape. He piled up 1,229 receiving yards and 19 touchdowns as a senior at Calera High School, earning consensus four-star billing and a spot among the top 15 wide receivers nationally by recruiting composite before he picked Alabama over Maryland.

“Fluid, fast receiver with elite change of direction skills and good ball skills,” scout Charles Power wrote of Prentice’s game, as reported by On3.

He never quite broke through with the Crimson Tide. Prentice caught 60 passes for 780 yards and five touchdowns across three seasons in Tuscaloosa, flashing big-play speed with a 47-yard touchdown against Kansas State and a 79-yard score against Arkansas but never cracking the every-down lineup, according to Alabama’s official athletics site.

A transfer to Baylor finally unlocked him. Prentice caught 26 passes for 380 yards and six touchdowns in his lone season with the Bears, scoring in all six of his first six games and hauling in a 73-yard touchdown at Oklahoma State. It was the most productive stretch of his college career.

Still, no team drafted him in April. Carolina signed him to a modest rookie deal, only to release him a day before the Patriots claimed him, according to RotoWire staff.

Read More From Heavy Patriots Trade Pitch Sends Kayshon Boutte for 2-Time Pro Bowl Tight End

New England has been openly auditioning receiver depth and return options all week, bringing in tryout players including Keagan Johnson and Casey Washington before turning to Prentice instead, according to Reiss.

The Patriots aren’t looking for a finished receiver. They’re chasing raw athleticism. A 4.39-second 40-yard dash, a 36-inch vertical and a track background that includes a sub-11-second 100 meters makes for the kind of profile teams covet for kickoff and punt-return duty, according to draft evaluator DraftScout.

Prentice arrives immediately competing for a bottom-of-the-roster spot or a practice-squad gig, and the Patriots will lean on training-camp reps and preseason snaps to find out whether his college burst translates to the NFL. Kick return duty looks like his fastest path onto the field early.

For a team still auditioning its receiver room deep into July, adding a cheap, explosive undrafted rookie costs almost nothing. Whether Prentice sticks past Labor Day depends entirely on what training camp reveals over the next several weeks.

title: 5 Biggest Winners and Losers From Brickyard 400 Qualifying
description: Carson Hocevar grabbed the pole at Indianapolis, but Saturday's qualifying session produced several surprises throughout the field. Here are the five biggest winners and losers heading into the Brickyard 400.
fullText:
Saturday’s qualifying session at Indianapolis Motor Speedway did more than determine the starting lineup for Sunday’s Brickyard 400.

It also created clear winners and losers before a single lap of the race has been completed.

Carson Hocevar delivered another statement performance for Spire Motorsports by winning the pole, while several championship contenders were left with considerably more work to do on one of NASCAR’s toughest tracks to pass.

Here are the five biggest winners and losers from Brickyard 400 qualifying.

There was no bigger winner than Hocevar.

The Spire Motorsports driver put together the fastest lap of qualifying, edging Daniel Suárez to earn the pole for one of NASCAR’s crown jewel races.

Starting from the front at Indianapolis is always valuable, and Hocevar now has the first opportunity to control Sunday’s race heading into Turn 1.

Suárez came up just short of the pole, but a front-row starting spot means a Spire Motorsports sweep.

The veteran has shown flashes of speed throughout the season, and beginning Sunday’s race alongside Hocevar puts him in position to challenge for one of the biggest victories of his Cup Series career.

Making just another Cup Series appearance, Heim quietly turned one of the strongest qualifying laps of the afternoon.

The 23XI Racing development driver will roll off seventh, giving him an excellent opportunity to gain valuable experience while racing near the front of the field against NASCAR’s biggest stars.

Elliott’s qualifying run left him with plenty of work to do.

The Hendrick Motorsports driver will start 27th, meaning he’ll have to navigate traffic for much of the afternoon if he hopes to contend for the win.

Passing has historically been difficult at Indianapolis, making track position especially important.

Wallace finds himself in a similar situation.

The 23XI Racing driver qualified 29th, leaving him buried in the pack despite entering one of NASCAR’s biggest races of the season.

With strategy and clean air often deciding races at Indianapolis, Wallace will need to make up ground quickly to avoid spending much of the afternoon mired in traffic.

Here is where the field will take the green flag for Sunday’s Brickyard 400:

Qualifying doesn’t hand out trophies, but it often shapes the race at Indianapolis. Hocevar, Suárez and Heim enter Sunday with the advantage of prime track position, while drivers like Elliott and Wallace will have to rely on strategy, pit execution and timely passes to climb through the field.

title: The offense, it’s offensive: Yankees 3, Phillies 1
description: Getting a hit with runners in scoring position? Please…
fullText:
When the Phillies struggle on offense as a collective, there is usually a simple recipe for it:

Everyone starts pressing and swinging at bad pitches

The offense is in the middle of one of those stretches right now where everyone is trying to do too much, swinging at bad pitches, trying to hit a seven run home run and now, we have a four game losing streak.

And tonight, they even struck first! Trea Turner gets hit by a pitch, Kyle Schwarber doubles, newly shorn Bryce Harper hits a sacrifice fly and all of a sudden, there is a 1-0 Phillies lead and a runner on third base. Little did we know that that was the only run that would be scored on the evening.

On the mound, Tim Mayza was the opener and did a fine job over two shutout innings, giving way to Brian Keller in his major league debut. Keller did give up a home run to Austin Wells, but for the most part, did just fine in keeping the Yankees off the board, only allowing a single run over three innings. Clearly, the coaching staff did not want Keller out there too long, instead opting to go to the bullpen in the sixth inning instead.

In that inning, Kyle Backhus walked the first hitter he faced before getting the next two on strikeouts, giving way to Seth Johnson. Johnson looked like a decent candidate to break out as a reliever, but it just has not come to fruition. He gave up back to back hits to allow Wells to score and give the Yankees the lead.

Meanwhile, the offense was generating some traffic against Weathers, but couldn’t push anything across. In the sixth, they got runners on the corners with Bryan de la Cruz and J.T. Realmuto each singling, but facing Angel Chivilli, Bryson Stott popped out into foul territory to end the threat. The Yankees tacked on another in the seventh on a Jasson Dominguez home run and that was basically that.

The offense is just slumping so badly right now and everyone is trying to swing their way out of it. The Yankees have been pitching well prior to this series and have carried it over into Philadelphia, but still, there should be better at bats coming from this lineup. They’ll try and salvage a game tomorrow night on Sunday Night Baseball with Cristopher Sanchez on the mound, so we’ll see.

title: MVP Magarity Leads North to 12-8 Win in 2026 Senior All-American Women’s Game
description: (Inside Lacrosse Photo: Sean Sadayasu) Defense was in the air at Johnny Unitas Stadium on the campus of Towson University as the North topped the South 12-8, the second-lowest scoring game in All-America history (surpassed only by the South’s 10-9 OT win in 2018). For her five-save effort, first half
fullText:
(Inside Lacrosse Photo: Sean Sadayasu)

Defense was in the air at Johnny Unitas Stadium on the campus of Towson University as the North topped the South 12-8, the second-lowest scoring game in All-America history (surpassed only by the South’s 10-9 OT win in 2018).

For her five-save effort, first half North goalie Maeve Magarity (Penn Charter, Pa. / Boston College) was named the Gatorade Player of the Game, the first goalie in the women’s game history to earn that distinction.

“It feels awesome, I’m so grateful and thankful,” Magarity said on the broadcast when informed of her selection. “I can’t even put it into words [being the first goalie to be named MVP]. This is something every little girl dreams of, so to be able to accomplish it is something I’ll never forget.”

Cece Powell (Marcellus, N.Y. / North Carolina) got the North on the board five seconds into the game with a free position shot, but the game was nip-and-tuck for the next six minutes as Maria Bragg (Severna Park, Md. / Florida) and Isabel Insley (Roland Park, Md. / Princeton) gave the South its lone lead of the game, but Ava Obloj (West Islip, N.Y. / Florida) and Anna Christie (St. Anthony’s, N.Y. / Notre Dame) put the North back up by one.

Over the next nine minutes, the North broke the game open, scoring six goals in a nine-minute span, highlighted by Emma Speed (St. Anthony’s, N.Y. / Florida) and Caitlin Barnes (Islip, N.Y. / Boston College) scored unassisted goals to punctuate the run.

Twice in the second half, the South was able to cut the deficit to four goals, but only got it to three after Emma McCarthy (Paul VI, Va. / North Carolina) assisted Kylie Waters (Milton, Ga. / Clemson) with 1:07 to go, but Obloj finalized the scoreline with :08 to play.

The South was led by eight saves and just three goals allowed from Reagan O’Donovan (McDonogh, Md. / Penn State), Insley led the scoring with three goals and an assist, while Waters and Bragg each scored twice and Kenzie Rassas (Georgetown Visitation, Md. / Notre Dame) had a goal and an assist.

The North got two goals each from Powell, Barnes and Obloj, as well as two assists from Casey Cummings (Nyack, N.Y. / Syracuse). The most eye-popping stats, however, came from Sabrina Asadurian (Wantagh, N.Y. / Stony Brook), who finished with five caused turnovers and six groundballs.

Check back for standouts and evaluations from the ILWomen staff.

title: (Video) Forgotten Liverpool man serves timely reminder to Iraola with sumptuous 72nd-minute moment
description: Liverpool began their pre-season programme with an entertaining 4-2 win over Sunderland, with the lead changings hands twice in Nashville.An early Kieran Morrison goal fired the Reds in front before R...
fullText:
Liverpool began their pre-season programme with an entertaining 4-2 win over Sunderland, with the lead changings hands twice in Nashville.

An early Kieran Morrison goal fired the Reds in front before Regis Le Bris’ side netted either side of half-time.

Dominik Szoboszlai then scored a superb equaliser, with further goals from Federico Chiesa and Lewis Koumas ensuring victory in Andoni Iraola’s first game as LFC head coach.

The Italian’s strike to put Liverpool 3-2 ahead in the 72nd minute was brilliantly taken, with our number 14 producing a first-time finish from a tight angle to beat the goalkeeper.

The assist was every bit as good, with Calvin Ramsay receiving the ball on the right flank and taking a moment before picking out a delightful pass inside to Chiesa which took out three Sunderland defenders.

(Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images)

The Scottish right-back had become something of a forgotten man under Arne Slot, who was openly reluctant to use him last season despite the recurring injury problems the Reds had in that position.

The 22-year-old’s only first-team minutes in 2025/26 came in the Carabao Cup defeat to Crystal Palace and as a late substitute against Brighton in the FA Cup (Transfermarkt), which seems staggering considering how frequently both Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley were injured.

The latter will remain sidelined for some time yet, while the Dutchman endured a difficult evening in Nashville, losing his balance in the build-up to Sunderland’s second goal and carelessly coughing up possession in a dangerous area earlier in the match.

With his sublime assist for Chiesa, Ramsay served a timely reminder of what he can offer to Liverpool when given the opportunity, and he might have done enough to earn a start in our next match against Wrexham in midweek.

The Scot may be our third-choice right-back ordinarily, but Bradley’s injury has moved him closer to first-team contention, and all he can do is make the most of whatever game-time is afforded to him by Iraola.

title: Cincinnati Bengals’ B.J. Hill Injury Opens Door for Former Second-Round Pick
description: The Cincinnati Bengals received their first notable injury update before training camp opened.But the meaning of the move depends far more on how long B.J. Hill remains sidelined.The Bengals placed Hill on the active/physically unable to perform list Saturday, leaving one of their most reliable defensive linemen unavailable when practices begin.
fullText:
The Cincinnati Bengals received their first notable injury update before training camp opened.

But the meaning of the move depends far more on how long B.J. Hill remains sidelined.

The Bengals placed Hill on the active/physically unable to perform list Saturday, leaving one of their most reliable defensive linemen unavailable when practices begin.

The team did not disclose the injury or provide a timetable in its official roster announcement, which noted rookie tight end Josh Kattus as injured as well.

Cincinnati rebuilt the defensive interior during the offseason, giving the coaching staff enough veteran depth to survive a short Hill absence while offering Kris Jenkins Jr. a chance to reclaim ground in a suddenly crowded rotation.

CINCINNATI, OHIO – JANUARY 04: B.J. Hill #92 of the Cincinnati Bengals taps Shedeur Sanders #12 of the Cleveland Browns for a sack during the second quarter of the game at Paycor Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images)

Players placed on the active/PUP list can be activated at any point during camp once medically cleared, so Hill is not locked into missing regular-season games.

The calendar becomes more important if he remains unavailable near final cuts. Hill would move to reserve/PUP if he is not activated before Cincinnati establishes its 53-man roster, which would keep him out for at least the first four games.

There is also recent precedent for patience.

Hill began last year’s camp with a foot injury, then returned in time to start all 17 regular-season games.

He finished 2025 with 66 tackles and four sacks, but his run defense offered the greater value.

The Bengals’ official defensive tackle preview credited Hill with a 68.0 PFF run-defense grade, 17th among defensive tackles with at least 100 snaps. His 43 total tackles ranked seventh among 134 qualified interior defenders, while he missed only one tackle across 316 run-defense snaps.

Cincinnati needs that stability after allowing an NFL-high 2,500 rushing yards last season.

The Bengals added star power to the front, though Hill remains the returning veteran with the most experience in Cincinnati’s defensive rotation.

EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – OCTOBER 13: Kris Jenkins Jr. #90 of the Cincinnati Bengals in action during the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on October 13, 2024 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

The offseason additions of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen reduce the immediate danger of Hill missing practice time.

Lawrence arrives with 30.5 career sacks and three Pro Bowl selections, while Allen owns 45.5 career sacks and two Pro Bowl appearances.

The Bengals built the group around a three-man veteran rotation featuring Lawrence, Allen and Hill. An A to Z Sports projected depth chart listed all three as starters, with Jenkins among the primary backups.

Hill’s absence should move Jenkins closer to first-team work during the opening practices. The 2024 second-round pick played 498 snaps across 14 games last season, yet the likelihood of larger role waned after Cincinnati invested heavily in Lawrence and Allen.

Training camp now gives Jenkins a window to show he belongs in the weekly rotation rather than fighting for leftover snaps.

He can also strengthen his roster position as the Bengals decide how many defensive tackles to carry behind their veteran trio.

The same opportunity extends to the rest of Cincinnati’s young interior depth, but Jenkins has the draft pedigree and experience to receive the first extended look.

Hill’s placement becomes major news only if the absence stretches toward the end of August. Because an early return would turn the transaction into a temporary camp note that gave younger players useful work.

A prolonged stay on the sideline would remove a dependable run defender in Hill from a unit expected to lead Cincinnati’s defensive turnaround.

For now, Hill’s absence gives Jenkins a chance to prove he belongs in Cincinnati’s rotation.

title: Nick Martinez and 3 relievers pitch AL-best Rays to 3-0 win over slumping Guardians
description: Nick Martinez threw six sharp innings, Yandy Díaz became the fourth player in Tampa Bay history to reach 1,000 hits and the Rays shut out the slumping Cleveland Guardians 3-0 on Saturday night.  Junior Caminero hit an RBI double in the fifth to put Tampa Bay up 1-0 before Cedric Mullins extended the lead with a sacrifice fly.  Hunter Feduccia added a sacrifice bunt in the sixth that scored Victor Mesa Jr.
fullText:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Nick Martinez threw six sharp innings, Yandy Díaz became the fourth player in Tampa Bay history to reach 1,000 hits and the Rays shut out the slumping Cleveland Guardians 3-0 on Saturday night.

Junior Caminero hit an RBI double in the fifth to put Tampa Bay up 1-0 before Cedric Mullins extended the lead with a sacrifice fly. Hunter Feduccia added a sacrifice bunt in the sixth that scored Victor Mesa Jr.

The Rays have the best record in the American League at 61-43 and lead the AL East by two games over the New York Yankees.

Tanner Bibee pitched six innings and All-Star rookie Travis Bazzana had two of Cleveland's five hits as the Guardians lost their fourth consecutive game.

Díaz reached the milestone with his leadoff single in the first and finished 2 for 4 with a run. Carl Crawford holds the franchise record with 1,480 hits.

Martinez (10-2) struck out five and walked none. He allowed four hits and lowered his ERA to 2.45 over 117 1/3 innings in his first season with Tampa Bay.

Cole Sulser and Garrett Cleavinger each pitched an inning before All-Star closer Bryan Baker worked a one-hit ninth for his 27th save.

Bibee (4-10) permitted nine hits while striking out five and walking two. He threw 107 pitches, two shy of his career high.

In a matchup of All-Star pitchers, Guardians LHP Parker Messick (8-5, 2.68 ERA) faces RHP Drew Rasmussen (8-5, 3.28) in the series finale Sunday.

title: Ohio State basketball shares video to get to know Anthony Thompson
description: The Ohio State creative team dropped a video to help Buckeye Nation get to know 5-star freshman Anthony Thompson. Watch it here.
fullText:
I feel like what the Ohio State basketball team could be this year is flying a little bit under the radar. The Buckeyes retained John Mobley Jr. and Amare Bynum, are getting a talented big man back in the mix with Baylor transfer Josh Ojianwuna coming back from injury after being out all last year, and have a super-talented freshman forward in Ohio product Anthony Thompson coming into the program.

That last point is something that could make Ohio State a lot more dangerous than people give it credit for. Thompson has the height, length, and skill set to be a force on both sides of the court and should be one of the best players in the Big Ten almost immediately, and has a real shot at being an NBA draft lottery pick when he comes out.

Still, though, he's just an incoming freshman, so there's not a whole lot Buckeye Nation knows about the 6-foot, 8-inch versatile wing player. Because of that, the Ohio State creative team shared a video for OSU fans to get to know Thompson a little bit more, and we have it here for you for just that purpose.

When asked what type of player he is, Thompson responded, "I'm very versatile; I can do a lot of different things on the court offensively and defensively, and I'd say something that sets me apart from a lot of other players is my ability to shoot the ball and space the floor ... you should expect a player that works really hard on both sides of the floor, on and off the court, and you know, when it's time to play, a person that's going to give its all for Buckeye Nation."

Ohio State head coach Jake Diebler is also ready to unwrap the gift that is Thompson this year.

"We're excited about Anthony joining our program. He's got an ability to score at multiple levels," said Diebler. "He's got maturity. He's fun to be around, plays with joy, and we're excited for who he is just as much as what he can do on the court ... He's coming in with great size, great athleticism, and his ability to create both for himself and for others should be a real asset for us."

The first McDonald’s All American for the Buckeyes since D’Angelo Russell 🌰 

Buckeye Nation, get to know Anthony Thompson 🗣️@ant_thompson26 | #GoBucks pic.twitter.com/APO7EPIXLV

— Ohio State Hoops (@OhioStateHoops) July 21, 2026

I'd say Ohio State fans are also excited about who and what Thompson is for this team and can't wait to see the product on the court and what it means for the Buckeyes for the 2026-27 season. Maybe the only folks not excited for him are the opposing coaches and players that have to compete against him.

title: Multiple Jets Players Will Start Training Camp With Injuries
description: Multiple New York Jets players including nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat will be starting training camp injured. The post Multiple Jets Players Will Start Training Camp With Injuries appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Jets will deal with some adversity at the beginning of training camp.

Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic revealed that nose tackle T’Vondre Sweat “is going on the NFI list to start training camp with a hamstring injury. It’s not considered serious.”

“WR Tim Patrick and EDGE Tyler Baron will be placed on the PUP list at the start of camp as well. Patrick isn’t expected to be out long,” Rosenblatt added.

DT T'Vondre Sweat is going on the NFI list to start training camp with a hamstring injury. It's not considered serious, per source.

WR Tim Patrick and EDGE Tyler Baron will be placed on the PUP list at the start of camp as well. Patrick isn't expected to be out long, per…

— Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) July 25, 2026

The team confirmed the news on social media. On Saturday, July 25, the Jets’ rookies reported for training camp. On Tuesday, July 28, the Jets’ veterans will report, and the first training camp practice will be held on Wednesday, July 29.

Sweat was placed on the NFI list to start camp. What does that mean?

The NFI list stands for “Non-Football-Injury or Illness,” and “it is used for players who suffered injuries or ailments outside of NFL activities,” according to NFL senior researcher Anthony Holzman-Escareno.

In other words, this means that Sweat got hurt somewhere between mandatory minicamp in the middle of June and training camp beginning here in late July.

The good news is that it isn’t considered serious, according to Rosenblatt. That is a huge sigh of relief.

Sweat is going to be a key straw that stirs the drink for the Jets’ defense. Especially when it comes to run defense, which is an area the team struggled in last season.

Patrick and Baron are dealing with an entirely different situation. They were both placed on the “active/physically unable to perform list,” according to Jets team reporter Ethan Greenberg.

“Players are placed on this list during training camp and count toward a team’s 90-man roster. Players can be removed from the list at any time during camp, but can’t be placed back on the list. Players on this list as of final roster cutdowns must be placed on the Reserve/PUP, released, traded or counted against the 53-man roster,” Holzman-Escareno wrote.

Patrick isn’t expected to be out long, according to Rosenblatt. He has a clear path to one of the top six wide receiver spots on the roster. Patrick will serve in the wise sage mentor role and as an occasional spot filler in case of emergency.

There was no update on Baron’s status from Rosenblatt.

Baron hurt his knee during the Week 14 contest against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, December 7, last season. Shortly after that game, he was placed on injured reserve, ending his rookie campaign. He could still be recovering from that issue.

This is troubling news for Baron. The former Miami product is 24 and will turn 25 during the 2026 season.

He appeared in six games, but didn’t make a start. Baron only appeared in 95 defensive snaps, per Pro Football Reference.

Before this news, Baron appeared to have long odds to make the Jets’ 53-man roster. This only complicates the path to making some noise. If he has any shot of changing his football destiny, Baron has to get back on the football field as quickly as possible.
